name: Linear
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (user authorizes the Zapier app in Linear; Linear docs note issues created via Zapier are attributed to the 'Zapier' app, i.e. app-level OAuth actor)
webhook_sub_endpoint: GraphQL mutation webhookCreate(input: { url, teamId, resourceTypes: ["Issue", ...] }) against api.linear.app/graphql; also configurable in Settings > API UI. Scope = one team or all public teams
event_filtering: per-subscription resourceTypes array (PascalCase entity types) + team scope; action (create/update/remove) arrives as a payload field, not a subscription filter
signature_scheme: Linear-Signature header: hex HMAC-SHA256 of raw request body with per-webhook signing secret; Linear-Timestamp header + webhookTimestamp body field (ms epoch) for replay protection
retry_disable_policy: Fails on non-200, unreachable, or >5s response; retried max 3 times with backoff at 1 minute, 1 hour, 6 hours; persistently failing webhooks may be disabled by Linear and must be manually re-enabled
dedup_mechanism: Linear-Delivery header: UUIDv4 unique per payload; webhookId field in body identifies the subscription
learnings: Copy Linear's delivery contract wholesale: hex HMAC-SHA256 of raw body in one header, a per-delivery UUID header for dedup, and a timestamp for replay defense - it is the cleanest of the six. Entity-type-array filtering (resourceTypes) plus a create/update/remove action field keeps the subscription vocabulary small while staying expressive. Avoid its thin retry budget (3 attempts over ~7h) and silent auto-disable; attune should notify or expose disable state via API.

name: Jira Software Cloud
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Atlassian 3LO: log in, pick site, grant; directory page lists requested scopes read:jira-user read:jira-work read:attachment:jira read:sprint:jira-software etc.; some legacy operations additionally ask for a Jira API token field)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /rest/api/3/webhook (OAuth2 apps; url + webhooks with events array + JQL filter, expires after 30 days, extend via PUT /rest/api/3/webhook) or POST /rest/webhooks/1.0/webhook (admin webhooks; {name, url, events:[...], filters:{"issue-related-events-section": "<JQL>"}, excludeBody, secret})
event_filtering: per-subscription events array (or all events) plus declarative JQL scoping to restrict which issues fire the webhook
signature_scheme: Admin/REST webhooks: X-Hub-Signature header, format method=signature e.g. sha256=<hex HMAC> (WebSub-style, HMAC of body with the registration secret). OAuth2-app webhooks instead carry a JWT bearer token in Authorization signed with the app's client secret
retry_disable_policy: Retries up to 5 times on 425/429/5xx or connection failure/timeout, each retry delayed 5-15 minutes with randomized backoff; REST-registered webhooks expire after 30 days unless refreshed; failed webhooks retrievable via 'Get failed webhooks' API; X-Atlassian-Webhook-Flow header marks Primary vs Secondary (bulk-operation) deliveries
dedup_mechanism: X-Atlassian-Webhook-Identifier header: unique per webhook event within tenant and stable across retries (documented as the retry filter key); X-Atlassian-Webhook-Retry header carries current retry count
learnings: Copy the X-Atlassian-Webhook-Identifier pattern: a delivery id that is explicitly stable across retries plus a retry-count header is the most precise dedup contract found in this batch. The namespaced snake_case vocabulary (jira:issue_created) also matches attune's likely style. Avoid the 30-day expiry-and-refresh treadmill - it is almost certainly why Zapier ships Jira with zero Instant triggers (all four visible triggers are polling despite Jira having webhooks) - and avoid split registration paths with different auth/signature semantics.

name: Asana
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (help doc: 'Log into Asana to authenticate. Grant Zapier permission to access your account')
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/webhooks with resource (gid), target (URL), and optional filters array; requires webhooks:write scope; creation completes only after an X-Hook-Secret handshake the target must echo with 200/204
event_filtering: per-subscription filters array of structured objects {resource_type, resource_subtype, action, fields} - down to field-level granularity; filters are mandatory for webhooks on team/portfolio/goal/workspace resources; events matching any filter are delivered (OR semantics)
signature_scheme: X-Hook-Signature header: HMAC-SHA256 of request body using the per-webhook X-Hook-Secret shared during the creation handshake
retry_disable_policy: Target must answer within 10 seconds; on failure Asana retries with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours, then the webhook is deleted; webhook object exposes delivery_retry_count, next_attempt_after, failure_deletion_timestamp, last_success_at; heartbeat events keep liveness observable
dedup_mechanism: No delivery-id header documented; events are batched (multiple events per POST) and described by the events schema; consumers rely on event content plus last_success_at bookkeeping
learnings: Copy the X-Hook-Secret handshake: it proves endpoint ownership at subscribe time and establishes a per-webhook secret in one flow - a good fit for attune's public subscription API. The structured filter object (resource_type + action + fields) is the most granular filtering model in this batch and worth studying if attune wants field-level event noise control. Avoid hard-deleting subscriptions after a 24h outage; prefer ClickUp-style suspend/reactivate so consumers do not silently lose their subscription.

name: Trello
zapier_auth: OAuth-style token authorization (help doc: 'Log into Trello to authenticate. Grant Zapier permission... Click Yes, Continue to Trello' - Trello's API key + user token model behind an authorize screen)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.trello.com/1/tokens/{APIToken}/webhooks/?key={APIKey} with {callbackURL, idModel, description}; Trello sends an HTTP HEAD to callbackURL at creation and refuses the webhook unless it returns 200
event_filtering: all-events-per-model: a webhook is bound to one model (board/card/list/member) via idModel and fires for ANY action touching that model; no event-type filter at subscription time - consumers filter on the action.type in the payload
signature_scheme: X-Trello-Webhook header: base64 HMAC-SHA1 of (raw request body concatenated with the callbackURL) keyed with the application's secret
retry_disable_policy: 3 retries with 30s / 60s / 120s backoff, then stops; webhook is deleted when the callback returns HTTP 410 Gone, when the bound token is revoked/expires, or via the DELETE route; webhook object tracks consecutiveFailures and firstConsecutiveFailDate
dedup_mechanism: None documented; X-Trello-Client-Identifier header echo exists for attributing which client caused the action, not for delivery dedup
learnings: Mostly an anti-pattern list for attune: model-scoped all-events firehose without event-type filtering pushes all filtering cost to consumers (visible in Zapier - only 4 of 14 triggers could be made Instant), and HMAC-SHA1 keyed with an app-global secret over body+callbackURL is dated and awkward to verify. Do copy two ideas: HTTP 410 as a consumer-initiated unsubscribe signal, and the HEAD-check at creation as a cheap URL-validity gate (though Asana's echo handshake is stronger).

name: monday.com
trigger_examples: Any Column Value Changed in Board (Instant)
Specific Column Value Changed in Board (Instant)
zapier_auth: API key (help doc: 'In the API Token field, enter your personal access token')
webhook_sub_endpoint: GraphQL mutation create_webhook(board_id: ID!, url: String!, event: WebhookEventType!, config: JSON) - one event type per webhook, board-scoped; requires webhooks:write scope; also configurable via the board Automations Center UI; URL must answer a challenge echo at creation
event_filtering: single event type per subscription (WebhookEventType enum), board-scoped; a config JSON refines some events (e.g. change_specific_column_value takes {"columnId": ...}); subscribing to N event types requires N webhooks
signature_scheme: JWT in Authorization header, verified against the app's Signing Secret - but only for webhooks created with an integration app token; ordinary board webhooks rely on the creation-time challenge echo ({"challenge": "<token>"} must be returned) and are otherwise unsigned
retry_disable_policy: Retries once a minute for 30 minutes, then gives up (no exponential backoff, no documented auto-disable)
dedup_mechanism: None documented; payload carries originalTriggerUuid but its dedup semantics are not specified
learnings: Avoid the one-event-per-subscription model: it multiplies webhook registrations and API calls (attune should accept an events array). Also avoid making payload signing an opt-in that depends on how the webhook was created - default deliveries being unauthenticated is a real gap. The challenge-echo URL verification is simple and worth considering as an alternative or complement to Asana's header handshake, and per-event config JSON (column-level filtering) shows how to bolt fine-grained filters onto a coarse event enum.

name: ClickUp
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (help doc: 'Log into ClickUp to authenticate. Grant Zapier permission to access your account')
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.clickup.com/api/v2/team/{team_id}/webhook with {endpoint, events: [...]} where events accepts "*" wildcard; optional space_id/folder_id/list_id/task_id narrow the location scope; per-webhook secret returned in the creation response; manage via PUT/DELETE /api/v2/webhook/{webhook_id}
event_filtering: per-subscription events array (camelCase nounVerb strings) with "*" wildcard for all events, combined with hierarchical location scoping (workspace > space > folder > list > task)
signature_scheme: X-Signature header: hex HMAC-SHA256 of request body using the per-webhook secret returned at creation
retry_disable_policy: Documented health lifecycle: active -> failing -> suspended. Failing = non-2xx or >7s response; up to 5 retries per event, then fail_count increments and that event is dropped (never resent); suspended at fail_count 100; responding 410 or 401 suspends immediately; success auto-resets to active and zeroes fail_count; reactivate via PUT /api/v2/webhook/{webhook_id}; no notification on status change
dedup_mechanism: Documented idempotency key formula: {{webhook_id}}:{{history_item_id}} (webhook_id and history_items[].id are in every payload body)
learnings: The best overall template for attune's subscription API: POST /team/{id}/webhook with an events array + "*" wildcard + resource scoping, a per-webhook HMAC-SHA256 secret returned at creation, and an explicitly documented active/failing/suspended lifecycle with 410/401 fast-suspend and PUT reactivation - this maps directly onto a POST /api/v1/webhooks {url, events[]} design. Its documented idempotency-key formula is also a practice worth copying (though a dedicated delivery-id header like Linear's is cleaner). Avoid dropping failed events permanently and avoid staying silent when a webhook is suspended.

name: Front
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Zapier help: 'Log into Front App to authenticate. Grant Zapier permission'; requires Front company admin)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only: 'application webhooks' are configured as a feature of a developer app on Front's Developers page (with a challenge/response URL validation handshake); 'rule webhooks' are configured through the rules UI. No public POST /webhooks REST endpoint.
event_filtering: no per-subscription event array: application webhooks receive the full fixed event set for shared inboxes (payload carries a 'type' field); rule webhooks filter via rule conditions instead
signature_scheme: application webhooks: x-front-signature = base64(HMAC-SHA256(app signing key, '{x-front-request-timestamp}:' + raw_body)); rule webhooks: X-Front-Signature = base64(HMAC-SHA1(API secret, raw_body))
retry_disable_policy: 5-second response timeout; 429/500/408/timeout retried up to 3 times; 429 is the documented back-off signal; after the last failed retry the webhook is auto-disabled and the app creator is emailed; no backfill of missed events (docs tell you to reconcile via the List Events polling API)
dedup_mechanism: no delivery-id header documented; event objects carry sequential never-reused IDs (evt_*, base-36 of a decimal counter) usable for ordering/dedup
learnings: Copy Front's timestamp-prefixed HMAC-SHA256 signature (defeats replay) and its explicit 429-means-back-off contract, plus the challenge/echo URL-validation handshake before activating a subscription. Also copy the pairing of webhooks with a polling /events API as the documented reconciliation path after retries are exhausted. Avoid the split-brain of two webhook systems with different signature algorithms (SHA256 vs SHA1) and no per-subscription event filter.

name: Help Scout
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Help Scout's Inbox API is HTTPS-only OAuth 2.0 with Authorization Code flow for third-party integrations like Zapier)
webhook_sub_endpoint: programmatic + dashboard: POST /v2/webhooks accepting {url, events: ["convo.assigned", ...], secret, payloadVersion: "V2", label, notification}; full CRUD (List/Get/Update/Delete Webhook); also configurable via Manage > Apps > Webhooks UI
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array ('events' field, enum of ~27 dot-namespaced types); one webhook carries N event types
signature_scheme: X-HelpScout-Signature = base64(HMAC-SHA1(secret, raw_json_body)); X-HelpScout-Event header carries the event name; signature computed on the raw escaped body
retry_disable_policy: success = 2xx; HTTP 410 causes the webhook to be deactivated/deleted; any other non-2xx is retried up to 10 times with increasing timeout between retries, then the event is discarded; the webhook is auto-deactivated after 10+ discarded events
dedup_mechanism: no delivery-id header documented; only X-HelpScout-Event + X-HelpScout-Signature headers; a 'notification' mode sends only the changed resource URI instead of the payload
learnings: This is the cleanest template for attune's subscription API: a single POST /v2/webhooks with url + events[] + caller-supplied secret + versioned payload (payloadVersion), dot-namespaced resource.action event names, and the HTTP-410-unsubscribes convention Zapier REST hooks expect. Copy the graduated retry-then-quarantine policy (N retries -> discard, M discards -> auto-disable). Avoid HMAC-SHA1 (use SHA256) and add a delivery-id header, which Help Scout lacks.

name: Freshdesk
zapier_auth: API key (Zapier help: requires your Freshdesk API key from profile settings, admin-only; paid Growth/Pro/Enterprise plan required)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only: no webhook-subscription endpoint in the public REST API; outbound webhooks exist only as a 'Trigger Webhook' action inside automation rules configured in the admin UI (callback URL + optional API-key auth + custom headers)
event_filtering: rule-condition based: each automation rule (on ticket create / ticket update) carries its own condition filters and fires one configured callback URL; no event-type array or subscription object
signature_scheme: none documented; endpoint authentication is opt-in via 'Requires authentication' (API key/basic) plus user-defined custom headers (e.g. X-Sample-CustomHeader1: VALUE)
retry_disable_policy: failed callbacks (non-2xx/3xx) are retried once every 30 minutes for a total of 48 calls; webhook requests are rate-limited to 1000/hour with overflow buffered; account admins get an email on failure with time and reason; no auto-disable documented
dedup_mechanism: none documented; outbound WhatsApp API mentions a customer-supplied external_reference_id echoed in webhook payloads, but rule webhooks have no delivery-id header
learnings: Freshdesk shows the cost of having no first-class subscription API: Zapier still gets Instant triggers, but ordinary customers must click through automation-rule UIs, and there is no signature, no event vocabulary, and no delivery id -- everything attune wants to avoid. Its one useful idea is the operational safety valve: an hourly webhook budget with buffering plus admin email alerts on failure. Do not copy the fixed 30-minute flat retry cadence (48 tries over 24h) -- exponential backoff is strictly better.

name: Gorgias
trigger_examples: (only a hidden/unpublished 'Ticket Created' polling trigger exists in the app definition; no publicly usable triggers)
zapier_auth: not stated in retrieved sources (Gorgias' own REST API authenticates with HTTP Basic: account email + API key, so the Zapier app most likely follows that; unverified)
webhook_sub_endpoint: programmatic: POST /api/integrations with body {name, type: "http", http: {url, method, headers, triggers: {"ticket-created": true, ...}, request_content_type, response_content_type}} -- webhooks are modeled as generic 'HTTP integrations' bound to ticket events; full CRUD on /api/integrations
event_filtering: per-integration boolean map: 'triggers' object with one boolean flag per event type (not an array); docs inconsistently show dash-form (ticket-created) in the tutorial and underscore-form (ticket_created) in the API reference example
signature_scheme: none documented for outbound HTTP-integration calls; requests carry whatever static headers you configure (e.g. your own API key header)
retry_disable_policy: not documented in retrieved sources
dedup_mechanism: not documented in retrieved sources
learnings: Gorgias is the cautionary tale: its Zapier app has zero public triggers (only 2 actions), so 'attune has a Zapier app' must mean triggers or it is near-useless for a signal-routing product. Its generic HTTP-integration model (webhook = an integration record with a boolean-per-event triggers map, templated URLs, arbitrary headers) is flexible but has no signature, no documented retry policy, and an event vocabulary whose dash vs underscore spelling drifts between docs -- exactly the kind of token instability attune's append-only source rule forbids. Prefer Help Scout/Chatwoot's events-array model.

name: Crisp
zapier_auth: token/API key: install the Zapier plugin from the Crisp marketplace, generate a token in plugin settings, paste it into the Zapier connection
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only: Website Hooks are configured in Crisp dashboard website settings (Advanced configuration > Web Hooks); Plugin Hooks are configured on a Crisp Marketplace plugin; no public REST subscription endpoint documented
event_filtering: per-hook event-namespace selection, gated by token scopes: each event namespace maps to a token scope+permission, and Plugin vs Website hooks have different allowed namespace matrices (Website Hooks get a reduced set)
signature_scheme: X-Crisp-Signature = HMAC-SHA256 over the string '[{X-Crisp-Request-Timestamp};{json_body_string}]' with your signing secret -- but signed on Plugin Hooks only; Website Hooks are unsigned (docs recommend a ?key=KEY URL parameter instead)
retry_disable_policy: non-200 responses are re-attempted later; X-Delivery-Attempt-Limit and X-Delivery-Attempt-Count headers expose the retry budget per request; if all attempts fail, all deliveries to the endpoint are paused for about a minute (events in that window are lost); Website Hooks get no retries at all
dedup_mechanism: no delivery-id header; payload carries website_id + event + timestamp, and message events carry a client 'fingerprint' field; attempt-count headers identify redeliveries of the same event
learnings: Copy Crisp's colon-namespaced event taxonomy with scope-gated filtering (event namespace -> required token scope) and the X-Delivery-Attempt-Count/Limit headers that make retry state observable to the receiver -- great for debugging. Avoid the two-tier trap where the easy tier (Website Hooks, what Zapier-style users reach first) is unsigned, unretried, and event-restricted; attune should have exactly one webhook tier with signing and retries for everyone. Note Crisp still ships 8/8 Instant Zapier triggers off this infrastructure.

name: Chatwoot
zapier_auth: n/a -- zapier.com/apps/chatwoot/integrations returns 404 and the Zapier v4 apps API has no Chatwoot entry; integrations are built with the generic 'Webhooks by Zapier' app instead
webhook_sub_endpoint: programmatic + dashboard: POST /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/webhooks with {url, name, subscriptions: ["conversation_created", ...]} authenticated via api_access_token header; response includes a server-generated per-webhook 'secret'; full CRUD (GET list, PATCH update, DELETE)
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array ('subscriptions' enum field); payload carries a top-level 'event' discriminator field
signature_scheme: X-Chatwoot-Signature = 'sha256=' + HMAC-SHA256(webhook_secret, '{timestamp}.{raw_body}') with X-Chatwoot-Timestamp (unix seconds) for replay protection; docs prescribe constant-time comparison and optional timestamp-age rejection
retry_disable_policy: not documented in retrieved sources (no retry schedule or auto-disable policy published)
dedup_mechanism: X-Chatwoot-Delivery header: unique delivery ID per webhook event (when available)
learnings: Chatwoot (attune's closest OSS analog) is the best single design to copy for the subscription API: account-scoped POST /api/v1/accounts/{id}/webhooks with a subscriptions[] enum, server-generated secret returned once, Stripe-style 'sha256=' timestamp-bound HMAC-SHA256 signature, and a dedicated X-*-Delivery dedup header. Its gap is equally instructive: no official Zapier app means every Zapier user hand-wires 'Webhooks by Zapier' + copies signatures manually -- shipping attune's own Zapier connector on top of this exact webhook shape is the differentiator. Also note the undocumented retry policy is a trust gap attune should not repeat.

name: Basecamp
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Basecamp 3 API supports only OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens; no API-key path exists)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /buckets/{projectId}/webhooks.json with {payload_url (HTTPS required), types: ["Todo","Todolist", ...]} (default all types); PUT /webhooks/{id}.json updates payload_url/types/active; project-scoped, not account-scoped
event_filtering: per-subscription array of RESOURCE types (Todo, Message, Comment...), not event kinds — every lifecycle event (created/updated/trashed/...) for a subscribed type is delivered; the event kind arrives as a snake_case `kind` field in the payload
signature_scheme: none — no HMAC signature documented; deliveries carry only User-Agent 'Basecamp3 Webhook' and X-Request-Id
retry_disable_policy: up to 10 attempts with exponentially growing intervals, then the webhook is deactivated; only 2xx counts as success; 3xx redirects are not followed
dedup_mechanism: numeric event `id` in payload plus X-Request-Id UUID header per delivery; recent_deliveries with full request/response readable via GET webhook
learnings: Copy: resource-scoped subscription (payload_url + types array) is the simplest workable programmatic shape, and exposing recent_deliveries on the webhook resource is great operator UX. Avoid: no HMAC signature at all (receivers can't authenticate Basecamp), and filtering by resource type rather than event kind forces receivers to re-filter on `kind` themselves.

name: Height
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Height API documents OAuth2 authorization-code flow for third-party apps; API also had secret_ API keys; Zapier directory does not state it explicitly)
event_filtering: unknown — delivery envelope carries a `type` field (resource.verb) and a `webhookId`, implying per-webhook subscriptions, but the subscription API shape was never mirrored (docs lived in a now-dead Notion page; the community OpenAPI mirror has a Webhooks tag with zero paths)
signature_scheme: none documented — a community receiver authenticates deliveries only by matching the payload's webhookId field
dedup_mechanism: event envelope has unique `id` and `model: "webhookEvent"` plus `webhookId`; `data.model` / `data.previousModel` carry new/old resource snapshots
learnings: Height shut down 2025-09-24; its Zapier listing (8 all-Instant triggers) outlived its docs — a warning that webhook API docs hosted on Notion evaporate, so attune should keep webhook docs in-repo/versioned. Its `resource.verb` event naming and `model`/`previousModel` old-new snapshot pair in the payload are worth copying; shipping webhooks without any HMAC signature is not.

name: Shortcut
zapier_auth: API key — Shortcut API only supports token auth (Shortcut-Token header, generated at app.shortcut.com/settings/account/api-tokens); no OAuth
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — one Outgoing Webhook configured at app.shortcut.com/settings/integrations/outgoing-webhook (URL + optional secret); no REST endpoint to create/manage webhooks
event_vocab_examples: epic/delete (entity_type + action fields, e.g. entity_type: "story", action: "update")
event_filtering: all-events-per-endpoint — fires on every Story/Epic create/update/delete (incl. comments, tasks, VCS-driven workflow-state changes); no event-type selection; receiver dispatches on actions[].entity_type/action
signature_scheme: Payload-Signature header, HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 request body, hex-encoded; only sent when a secret was configured (optional)
dedup_mechanism: UUID `id` per webhook event envelope; changed_at timestamp; actions[] each carry entity id
learnings: Shortcut is the anti-pattern proof for attune's Zapier goal: because its webhook is a dashboard-only, unfiltered firehose with no subscription API, its Zapier app has ZERO triggers — only actions. A programmatic REST-hook subscribe/unsubscribe endpoint with per-event filtering is a hard prerequisite for Instant Zapier triggers. Its optional-secret HMAC-SHA256 Payload-Signature is fine but should be mandatory in attune.

name: Wrike
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Wrike API v4 uses OAuth 2.0 authorization-code; permanent access tokens exist but are legacy)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/v4/webhooks (account scope), POST /folders/{folderId}/webhooks, POST /spaces/{spaceId}/webhooks — body: hookUrl, secret (optional), events [TaskCreated,AttachmentAdded,...] (default all), recursive, parameterisedEvents (conditional filters + extra payload fields), customItemTypes; GET/PUT(status=Active|Suspended)/DELETE /webhooks/{id}
event_filtering: per-subscription event array PLUS parameterized conditional filters (e.g. TaskCustomFieldChanged limited to specific customField IDs) and customItemTypes scoping; logic = CIT AND (events OR parameterisedEvents); an event may appear in events or parameterisedEvents, not both
signature_scheme: X-Hook-Signature: HMAC-SHA256(secret, request body) on every event; registration handshake sends X-Hook-Secret random challenge — receiver must echo HMAC-SHA256(secret, challenge) back in the response X-Hook-Secret header
retry_disable_policy: retryable statuses: up to 3 delivery attempts then webhook Suspended; non-retryable 4xx (all except 408 and 429) suspend immediately with no retries; author gets email on suspension; reactivate via PUT /webhooks/{id} status=Active
dedup_mechanism: Idempotency-Key request header carrying a unique identifier per event, explicitly documented for duplicate-delivery protection (at-least-once delivery)
learnings: Wrike has the most complete subscription API of the PM cohort — copy the explicit Idempotency-Key header, the Active/Suspended state machine with an un-suspend endpoint, and the challenge-response handshake that proves URL ownership at registration. Also note the irony: despite this rich webhook API its Zapier app still uses polling triggers, so attune must actually wire REST hooks into the Zapier app, not just ship the API.

name: Zendesk
zapier_auth: API key — subdomain + agent (admin) email + Zendesk API token, per Zapier's own help article
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/v2/webhooks with body {webhook: {name, endpoint, http_method: "POST", request_format: "json", status: "active", subscriptions: ["zen:event-type:ticket.created", ...]}}; signing secret via GET/POST /api/v2/webhooks/{id}/signing_secret
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (subscriptions field) — OR, mutually exclusively, the webhook is connected to a Zendesk trigger/automation with a custom JSON payload; a single webhook cannot do both
signature_scheme: X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature: base64(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + rawBody)) with the timestamp in a separate X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature-Timestamp header (ISO-8601); replay-protect by rejecting stale timestamps
retry_disable_policy: 409 retried up to 3 times; 429/503 honor Retry-After when under 60s; circuit breaker pauses delivery when error rate hits 70% or after 1,000+ errors in a 5-minute window
dedup_mechanism: CloudEvents-style envelope with unique event `id` (used as idempotency key), `type`, `time`, `subject` (e.g. zen:ticket:35436), `detail` snapshot and `event` diff
learnings: Zendesk's namespaced vendor-prefixed event vocabulary (zen:event-type:resource.verb) and signed-timestamp HMAC (timestamp+body, separate timestamp header) are the strongest security/naming pattern in this batch — attune should copy the timestamp-in-signature replay defense. The subscriptions-array-per-webhook endpoint is exactly the shape attune's Zapier REST hooks need. Its error-rate circuit breaker (70% / 1000-in-5-min) is a good scale-safe alternative to naive N-consecutive-failures disabling.

name: Intercom
zapier_auth: OAuth2 — log into Intercom and grant Zapier permission (per Zapier's help article)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — webhook URL + topic selection configured per app in the Developer Hub (app settings); saving triggers a signed `ping` handshake that must get a 2xx; no public REST subscription-management endpoint
event_filtering: per-app topic list (array of topics selected in the Developer Hub); one endpoint per app receives all selected topics; receiver dispatches on the envelope `topic` field
signature_scheme: X-Hub-Signature: sha1=<hex> — HMAC-SHA1 over the raw JSON body keyed by the app's client_secret (legacy GitHub-style; weak algorithm by modern standards)
retry_disable_policy: retries failed deliveries multiple times with backoff (exact schedule not documented in retrieved sources); envelope carries delivery_status and delivery_attempts fields
dedup_mechanism: unique notification `id` (notif_...) in every envelope, documented as the idempotency key; delivery_attempts counter exposes redelivery
learnings: Intercom proves all-Instant Zapier triggers (18/18) are achievable even with dashboard-only topic config — because Zapier is itself the OAuth app owning the subscription; but attune, wanting third parties to subscribe, should still prefer Zendesk-style programmatic subscriptions. Copy Intercom's dot-separated resource.actor.verb topic vocabulary, the uniform notification envelope with delivery_attempts, and the signed ping handshake; avoid HMAC-SHA1 — use SHA-256.

name: Frill
zapier_auth: API key (inferred from Frill API docs — Bearer / Basic / query-string api_key are the only schemes Frill's API supports; Zapier directory does not state auth)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (Settings > Webhooks); no programmatic subscription endpoint in public API reference, though Zapier's 4 Instant triggers imply a private REST-hook subscribe API
event_filtering: per-subscription event selection implied ("subscribe to certain events") but configured in dashboard; not documented as an events array on an API
signature_scheme: HTTP header `Signature` (no vendor prefix) = hex HMAC-SHA256 of JSON payload keyed with dashboard Webhook Secret; verified via hash_hmac('sha256', payloadJson, secret)
dedup_mechanism: none documented; envelope carries only triggered_at (UTC), event, data, data_type — no delivery id or event id
learnings: Copy Frill's clean noun.verb event vocabulary and its uniform envelope {triggered_at, event, data, data_type}, but avoid its mistakes: a bare `Signature` header (no product prefix, collision-prone), mixed casing (idea.statusChanged camelCase verb), signing the re-encoded JSON rather than the raw body, and no delivery-id/retry documentation. Also note the gap attune can beat: webhook config is dashboard-only while Zapier gets instant triggers, so a public REST-hook subscribe API is a differentiator.

name: Nolt
zapier_auth: API key (inferred from Nolt Public API — `apikey` header on the GraphQL endpoint is the only documented auth; Zapier directory does not state auth)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (board > Settings > Integrations > Webhooks; form fields: Endpoint URL, optional Verify token, optional Signing secret); public API is GraphQL at https://api.nolt.io/api/v1/graphql with no webhook mutations documented
event_filtering: all-events-per-endpoint — the webhook form has no event selection; every board event is delivered and the handler switches on the `event` field
signature_scheme: X-Hub-Signature: sha256={hex} — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body keyed with the Signing secret; plus a PubSubHubbub-style GET verification handshake (hub.mode=subscribe&hub.challenge&hub.verify_token) that the endpoint must echo before activation
retry_disable_policy: endpoint must return 200 OK within 5 seconds; on failure Nolt emails the board owner; continued failure may disable the webhook, owner re-enables manually after fixing; no backoff schedule documented
dedup_mechanism: none documented; body carries event, boardId, triggeredAt (ISO 8601), data — no delivery id
learnings: Nolt is the best small-scale reference for the GitHub-style conventions attune wants: X-Hub-Signature sha256= HMAC over raw body, a challenge/verify-token subscription handshake, and a stable {event, boardId, triggeredAt, data} envelope. Avoid its inconsistent event grammar (post.status.updated three-segment vs comment.created two-segment) and the missing delivery-id/retry-schedule; also note all-events-per-endpoint forces consumers to filter client-side — attune should carry an events array per subscription instead.

name: Upvoty
zapier_auth: API key (inferred — Upvoty API uses `Authorization: Bearer up_live_...` scoped keys per its API feature page; Zapier directory does not state auth)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-configured (register endpoint, choose events, per-endpoint filters); no public programmatic subscription endpoint documented, though Zapier's 4 Instant triggers imply a private REST-hook subscribe API
event_filtering: per-endpoint event-type selection plus attribute filters (board, tag, segment, vote count); multiple endpoints supported so different events can route to different URLs
signature_scheme: X-Upvoty-Signature header — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body with a shared secret, accompanied by a timestamp to prevent replay (explicitly modeled on Stripe); example shows value form sha256=...
retry_disable_policy: non-2xx triggers exponential backoff retries for up to 24 hours; every attempt logged with request/response/latency; after 24h of continuous failure the endpoint is marked degraded and the owner emailed — events are never silently dropped; dashboard supports one-click replay of any past delivery
dedup_mechanism: delivery/event replay via dashboard event log; no explicit delivery-id or idempotency header documented (payload schemas described as stable and versioned)
learnings: Upvoty's webhook surface (from its official product pages) is the richest checklist in this cohort: X-Upvoty-Signature HMAC-SHA256 + timestamp anti-replay, exponential backoff capped at 24h, degraded-endpoint email instead of silent disable, full delivery log with replay, per-endpoint event arrays plus attribute filters, and versioned payload schemas. attune should copy the retry/replay/observability posture and the timestamped signature; caveat: this is marketing copy, and the formal developer reference with the subscription endpoint shape is not publicly reachable, so verify header/value details before cloning exactly.

name: Sleekplan
zapier_auth: API key (inferred — Sleekplan REST API uses `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` from Settings > Developer; Zapier directory does not state auth)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (Settings > Developer > Webhooks > Add webhook, URL with recommended ?key=SECRET query param); no programmatic subscription API documented
event_filtering: all-events-per-endpoint — docs describe registering a URL and Sleekplan 'starts delivering events immediately'; no event selection documented; consumer switches on the `action` field
signature_scheme: none — docs explicitly state Sleekplan does not HMAC-sign payloads; recommended verification is a secret appended as a GET query parameter (?key=MY_SECRET_KEY) validated server-side
dedup_mechanism: none documented; envelope is {product_id, action, data, timestamp(ms)} with no delivery or event id
learnings: Sleekplan is the anti-pattern for attune's security story: no HMAC signature (secret-in-URL instead, which leaks via logs/referrers), no retry policy, no delivery id, and imperative-verb events (item.create) instead of past-tense. Its two good ideas are worth keeping: the `data` payload shape exactly mirrors the REST API resource representation (one schema to document), and its 14 instant Zapier triggers show that a wide event vocabulary maps 1:1 onto Zapier hook triggers cheaply.

name: featureOS (Hellonext)
zapier_auth: API key (inferred — featureOS API authenticates with an `API-KEY: hn_...` header; OAuth2 apps exist but the legacy HellonextCLIAPI Zapier app predates them; Zapier directory does not state auth)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard for org webhooks (Dashboard > Webhooks > Add Webhook: URL + description + event checkboxes); programmatic for OAuth apps: POST https://api.featureos.app/oauth/apps with webhook_url + subscribed_webhook_events[] (requires webhooks:manage scope), and per-install granted_webhook_events[] subset at consent
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array — dashboard webhooks select events at creation; OAuth apps declare subscribed_webhook_events and each installing org grants a subset (granted_webhook_events), auto-provisioning a webhook scoped to the granted events
signature_scheme: HMAC signing stated for the shared webhook pipeline, but header name and algorithm are not documented in the public pages retrieved
retry_disable_policy: 3 retries at fixed intervals of 5 minutes, 30 minutes, and 2 hours after a non-200; after all fail the webhook is disabled and the owner emailed; manual re-enable in Organization Settings > Webhooks; per-webhook retry logs viewable in dashboard
dedup_mechanism: none documented; payload is {type, data, created(unix)} with before/after diff objects for update events — no delivery id header
learnings: Two ideas worth copying: (1) the before/after diff block inside update payloads (status transitions carry both old and new values — exactly what a Zapier 'status changed to X' filter needs), and (2) the OAuth-app model where the app declares subscribed_webhook_events and each tenant grants a subset — a clean consent story for attune's connector. Avoid the vocabulary drift (snake_case post_created in the app API vs camelCase postCompleted in the classic payload `type`) and the fixed 3-retry-then-disable policy which is harsher than backoff-based peers.

name: Savio
zapier_auth: API token — Savio docs explicitly instruct including `Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN_VALUE` when using the API as a webhook target in Zapier
event_filtering: unknown — no outbound webhook or event system documented anywhere in Savio's public API reference
learnings: Savio is the inbound-only counterexample: its Zapier app is a single write action (Log Product Feedback) and its API is ingest/read REST with token auth — no outbound events at all, so a customer cannot react to feedback triage in their own tools. This validates attune's thesis that outbound webhook subscriptions plus instant Zapier triggers are the differentiating half of a connector; a create-feedback action alone is table stakes. Savio's one nice touch: a copy-paste 'API reference for AI assistants' block in its docs.

name: Canny
zapier_auth: API key (Secret API Key from Canny Settings > API; Owner-level admin required to authorize)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (configured in Your Subdomain > Settings > API; no public subscription REST endpoint documented — the Zapier CLI app evidently uses a private REST-hook subscribe API since all 5 triggers are Instant)
event_filtering: unknown — docs list a global vocabulary of 13 event types; no per-subscription event selection is documented
signature_scheme: canny-signature header = HMAC-SHA256 of the canny-nonce (NOT the body), keyed with the team API key, Base64-encoded; plus canny-timestamp (ms epoch, for replay protection) and canny-nonce (random, unique per request)
retry_disable_policy: not documented (no retry/backoff/disable policy anywhere in the API reference)
dedup_mechanism: canny-nonce header is unique per request and canny-timestamp guards replays; no explicit event-id dedup guidance
learnings: Copy: all visible triggers as Instant REST hooks plus a Find Post search and Create-or-Update User action for vote-on-behalf round-trips; envelope shape {created, object, objectType, type} with objectType.verb naming is clean. Avoid: signing only a nonce instead of timestamp+body (weaker integrity), leaving retry policy undocumented, and offering no public programmatic subscription endpoint while the Zapier app clearly uses a private one.

name: Productboard
zapier_auth: API token (Bearer) — Productboard API supports API token / OAuth2 / OAuth S2S JWT; Zapier directory does not state which explicitly, vendor help says Zapier maintains the integration on top of the public API
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.productboard.com/v2/webhooks with body {data:{fields:{name, events:[{eventType}], notification:{url (https, publicly resolvable, no loopback/private IPs), version:1, headers:{authorization}}}}}; also GET /v2/webhooks, GET/DELETE /v2/webhooks/{id}; requires webhooks:write scope
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (events: [{eventType}], at least one, no duplicates) validated against OAuth scopes
signature_scheme: no HMAC signature — subscriber authenticates deliveries via a customer-configured static Authorization header (notification.headers.authorization, any scheme) echoed on every delivery
retry_disable_policy: 5s end-to-end delivery timeout; any 2XX acknowledges (204 preferred); failed deliveries retried with exponential backoff up to 8 attempts (1m, 3m, 9m, ...); too many timeouts/failures may result in Productboard disabling the subscription with notification loss
dedup_mechanism: not documented — v1 payload carries entity id + eventType + links.target + updatedAttributes but no delivery/event id
learnings: Copy: the cleanest programmatic subscription contract in the cohort — named subscriptions, event-type array, explicit payload version field, URL validation (https + SSRF guard), documented backoff schedule and auto-disable, thin payload with links.target fetch-back plus updatedAttributes diff hints. Avoid: shipping without HMAC body signing (static auth header is weaker) and without a delivery/event id for dedup; also note their Zapier 'New X' triggers fall back to polling — attune should make created-events instant too.

name: UserVoice
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (Admin Console > Integrations > Service hooks; Admin API v2 only exposes read-only GET /admin/service_hook_logs for delivery logs)
event_filtering: per-hook event checkboxes chosen in dashboard, optionally restricted to specific forums; no dotted machine-readable event tokens documented
signature_scheme: 'signature' request parameter = HMAC-SHA256 over the 'data' parameter (JSON or XML payload), keyed with the account's SSO key — no dedicated header
retry_disable_policy: explicitly none — help doc FAQ: no auto-retry on failure; no bundling or rate limiting, individual events only
dedup_mechanism: none documented
learnings: Cautionary tale: zapier.com/apps/uservoice/integrations 404s and Zapier's app API returns zero results, so the listed slug no longer exists — a once-listed integration can disappear. Its service hooks are legacy design: dashboard-only, human-readable event names instead of stable tokens, signature keyed on the SSO key (credential reuse), and explicitly no retries. The per-forum event scoping is the one idea worth keeping (attune analog: per-source/tenant filters on a subscription).

name: Pendo
action_examples: (only hidden Create/Update Customer write; no visible actions or searches)
zapier_auth: API key / integration auth token (hidden 'Check Auth Token' test trigger in the app; underlying Feedback API authenticates with an 'auth-token' header carrying the Feedback integration key)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.feedback.us.pendo.io/hooks with JSON {target_url, event} (one event string per subscription); unsubscribe via POST /hooks/unsubscribe with {target_url}; auth-token header
event_filtering: one event type per subscription (subscribe call takes a single 'event' string; create one hook per event)
signature_scheme: none documented
retry_disable_policy: not documented
dedup_mechanism: not documented
learnings: The 'pendo' Zapier slug is actually Pendo Feedback (ex-Receptive, ReceptiveCLIAPI); the flagship Pendo product sits at pendo-legacy with only polling report triggers — evidence that a purpose-built REST-hook subscribe API (POST /hooks {target_url, event}) is exactly what makes instant Zapier triggers cheap to build. Copy the minimal subscribe/unsubscribe shape as the Zapier-facing surface, but avoid its gaps: no signature, no retry policy, no dedup, no list endpoint, and snake_case event names inconsistent with the industry object.verb style.

name: Sprig
zapier_auth: API key — environment-scoped 'Zapier API Key' (Development ID / Production ID from Sprig Integrations > Zapier > Get API Keys)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (Integrations > Destinations > Webhook > Configure: payload URL + Bearer token + event checkboxes, per Product and per Environment; includes a Test Webhook button)
event_filtering: per-configuration event checkboxes in dashboard (Answer submitted, Study submitted, Study sent, Study seen, Theme identified, Study status changed); one config per Product+Environment
signature_scheme: none — outbound requests carry a customer-set static Bearer token in the authorization header; no HMAC
retry_disable_policy: not documented
dedup_mechanism: numeric 'id' (webhook ID) field in the Answer Submitted payload; no formal delivery-id/dedup guidance
learnings: Minimal viable Zapier surface: a single Instant trigger with zero actions still ships value for a survey product, and environment-scoped API keys (dev vs prod ID) are a nice tenancy idea for attune. Avoid its event naming chaos — three parallel vocabularies (human labels, eventType snake_case, eventName camelCase) across payloads with inconsistent field docs; the built-in Test Webhook button is worth copying for DX.

name: Featurebase
zapier_auth: API key (Settings > Integrations > next to Zapier click Get API Key, paste into Zapier)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://do.featurebase.app/v2/webhooks with {name, url (https), description?, topics[], requestConfig?{timeoutMs, headers (max 10)}}; response includes signing secret 'whsec_...'; full CRUD: list/retrieve/update/delete plus refresh_secret rotation endpoint; max 10 endpoints per org; versioned via Featurebase-Version header (2026-01-01.nova); dashboard config also available
event_filtering: per-subscription topics array (subscribe to exactly the topics you need; ~28 topics across feedback, changelog, and conversation domains)
signature_scheme: X-Webhook-Signature = hex HMAC-SHA256 over '{timestamp}.{raw body}' keyed with the whsec_ secret, plus X-Webhook-Timestamp (Unix seconds); docs mandate 5-minute replay window and constant-time compare — Stripe-style
retry_disable_policy: up to 3 automatic retries at 1 minute, 1 hour, and 6 hours; failure = non-2xx, timeout, or connection failure; webhook objects carry a status field ('active') but no documented auto-disable threshold
dedup_mechanism: notification_event envelope with unique event id ('notif_<uuid7>'); docs explicitly instruct persisting processed IDs and skipping duplicates; ordering explicitly NOT guaranteed
learnings: The best end-to-end reference for attune's webhook-subscription API: programmatic CRUD + topics array + whsec_ secret returned at creation + rotation endpoint + Stripe-style timestamp.body HMAC + documented retry ladder + notif_ event-id dedup + explicit no-ordering contract + date-tagged API versioning. Ironically its Zapier triggers are plain polling — proving a great webhook API still needs the Zapier app wired to REST hooks to get the Instant badge; attune should do both.

name: Vercel
zapier_auth: API key (Vercel personal access token pasted into Zapier as 'Vercel API Token', optional Team ID field)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.vercel.com/v1/webhooks with JSON body {"url": "https://example.com", "events": [...], "projectIds": [...]} (Bearer token; optional ?teamId= query param). Response returns one-time secret + webhook id. Also GET list / GET one / DELETE. Dashboard config also available (Team Settings > Webhooks, Pro/Enterprise).
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (events[]) plus optional resource scoping via projectIds[]
signature_scheme: x-vercel-signature header, HMAC-SHA1 hex digest of the raw request body using the webhook secret (integration webhooks use the OAuth2 Client Secret); docs recommend constant-time comparison
retry_disable_policy: 30-second delivery timeout; non-2xx responses retried with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours, then the event is discarded (no documented auto-disable of the endpoint)
dedup_mechanism: Payload envelope carries 'id' documented as 'The ID of the webhook delivery' plus type/createdAt/region; consumers dedupe on id
learnings: Vercel is the cleanest minimal reference for attune: one POST /v1/webhooks endpoint taking url + events[] + resource-id scoping, secret returned exactly once at creation, envelope {id,type,createdAt,payload}. Copy the envelope + per-subscription events array; avoid copying HMAC-SHA1 (use SHA-256) and note their weak Zapier app (polling-only) shows shipping REST-hook triggers is a differentiator.

name: Netlify
zapier_auth: Not explicitly documented in directory/help (getting-started article 404s); Netlify API uses OAuth2 bearer tokens and the connection uses Zapier's standard 'Add connection' flow
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/v1/hooks?site_id={site_id} with body {site_id, type ("url"|"email"|"slack"), event, data:{url:...}}; GET /api/v1/hooks?site_id=, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/hooks/{hook_id}, POST /hooks/{hook_id}/enable, GET /hooks/types. Dashboard 'Deploy notifications' UI configures the same hooks.
event_filtering: one event per hook object (create N hooks for N events); no events-array per subscription
signature_scheme: X-Webhook-Signature header carrying a JWS (JWT, HS256) whose claims are {iss:"netlify", sha256:<hex SHA-256 of payload>}; only sent if a JWS secret is configured (optional)
retry_disable_policy: not documented in the deploy-notifications or API docs
dedup_mechanism: not documented (payload is a JSON representation of the deploy/submission object; consumers key on deploy id)
learnings: Netlify proves a tiny surface works: 4 all-Instant Zapier triggers built on one-event-per-hook subscriptions. The JWT-wrapped signature (X-Webhook-Signature JWS) is more complex for receivers than plain HMAC-hex — attune should prefer Stripe/HubSpot-style HMAC-SHA256. One-event-per-hook forces N subscriptions for N events; attune's events-array design is friendlier. Undocumented retry policy is a gap to avoid.

name: HubSpot
trigger_examples: CRM Object Recently Created or Updated (polling)
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into HubSpot in a popup and grant Zapier access)
webhook_sub_endpoint: Classic app webhooks: app-level settings (GET/PUT /webhooks/2026-3/{appId}/settings with {targetUrl, throttling.maxConcurrentRequests}) + per-event subscriptions (POST /webhooks/2026-3/{appId}/subscriptions, one eventType each; developer API key auth). New v4 model is pull-based: POST https://api.hubapi.com/webhooks-journal/subscriptions/v4 {objectTypeId, subscriptionType OBJECT|ASSOCIATION, actions [CREATE,UPDATE,DELETE], properties[], objectIds[]} with no targetUrl — the app polls a journal (GET /webhooks-journal/journal/v4/latest|earliest|offset/{offset}/next).
event_filtering: one targetUrl per app; one subscription object per event type (objectType.action), property-change subscriptions filter by propertyName; deliveries are batched arrays of up to 100 notifications per POST
signature_scheme: X-HubSpot-Signature (SHA-256 of app client secret + raw body); v3: X-HubSpot-Signature-v3 = base64(HMAC-SHA256(client_secret, method+uri+body+timestamp)) with X-HubSpot-Request-Timestamp, reject if older than 5 minutes
retry_disable_policy: retries on connection failure, >5s timeout, or any 4xx/5xx; up to 10 retries spread over 24 hours with randomized jitter; concurrency capped at maxConcurrentRequests (min >5, default 10)
dedup_mechanism: each notification carries eventId (explicitly 'not guaranteed to be unique'), subscriptionId, attemptNumber (starts at 0), occurredAt; v4 journal uses UUID offsets for exactly-once-style sequential consumption
learnings: HubSpot's dotted objectType.action vocabulary (contact.creation, deal.propertyChange, generic object.*) is the naming style attune should copy, and its payload fields (eventId, subscriptionId, occurredAt, attemptNumber) are a good envelope checklist. Its weaknesses are instructive: one target URL per app (not per subscription) and a non-unique eventId force awkward consumer dedup — attune should give each subscription its own URL+secret and a globally unique delivery id. Batched arrays (<=100 events/POST) are worth considering for burst efficiency.

name: Salesforce
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Salesforce and grant access; requires My Domain and Zapier approved as an External Client App; connected-app limit of 5 access tokens per account)
webhook_sub_endpoint: No generic public REST webhook-subscription endpoint. Push integrations are (a) Outbound Messages: SOAP/XML POSTs to a listener URL, configured through Workflow/Flow in Setup (dashboard-only) — this is what backs Zapier's one Instant trigger; (b) Change Data Capture / Platform Events consumed by subscribing to channels (e.g. /data/Employee__ChangeEvent) over Pub/Sub API (gRPC) or CometD — a streaming subscription, not an HTTP callback registration.
event_filtering: topic/channel-based: subscribe per object change-event channel; objects must be enabled for Change Data Capture in Setup; changeType + changedFields discriminate within the channel
signature_scheme: none documented for Outbound Messages (SOAP over HTTPS; receiver acks via SOAP response); CDC/Pub-Sub is an authenticated streaming connection so no per-delivery signature
retry_disable_policy: not retrieved from primary docs (developer.salesforce.com help pages are JS-rendered and blocked); not asserted here
dedup_mechanism: CDC events carry ChangeEventHeader with transactionKey, sequenceNumber, commitNumber and commitTimestamp for ordering/dedup; consumers replay streams from a position
learnings: Salesforce is the anti-pattern for attune's goal: no simple 'POST a URL + events' API, push requires SOAP Outbound Messages configured in the admin UI, and its Zapier app is consequently 8/9 polling. The lesson is that heavyweight enterprise eventing (gRPC Pub/Sub, replay ids) maximizes power but makes third-party Instant triggers rare; attune should ship the simple HTTP subscription Salesforce lacks. Its transactionKey/sequenceNumber ordering metadata is worth borrowing conceptually for dedup.

name: Pipedrive
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Pipedrive and grant Zapier access)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /v1/webhooks with JSON body {subscription_url (required, public HTTPS, no redirects, cannot be a Pipedrive API URL), event_action (required), event_object (required), user_id, http_auth_user, http_auth_password, name}; also manageable in-app at Settings > Tools and apps > Webhooks. Version field "2.0" selects Webhooks v2.
event_filtering: one action.object pair per webhook with wildcard support (*.* = all events); wildcards match all supported actions/objects — N precise pairs need N webhooks unless wildcarded
signature_scheme: no HMAC signature for general webhooks; receiver authentication is optional HTTP Basic auth via http_auth_user/http_auth_password on the subscription
retry_disable_policy: success = any 2XX within 10s; on failure retries 3 more times after 3s, 30s and 150s; repeated unreachability increments a ban counter (banned webhook's events are lost); webhook is deleted after 3 consecutive days with no successful delivery
dedup_mechanism: meta block on every payload: id (event ID), correlation_id, entity, action, entity_id, timestamp, attempt (delivery attempt number), is_bulk_edit, version
learnings: Pipedrive shows what powers a heavily-Instant Zapier app (11/18 Instant): a dead-simple POST /v1/webhooks and a two-part action.object event grammar with wildcards — attune's event vocabulary could adopt the same verb.noun style plus '*' support. Its meta block (event id + correlation_id + attempt + previous-vs-data diff) is an excellent envelope model. Avoid: Basic-auth-only delivery security (no HMAC) and the aggressive silent auto-delete after 3 bad days, which loses events without notification.

name: Mailchimp
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Mailchimp and grant Zapier access)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /lists/{list_id}/webhooks (Marketing API, per-audience) to create; GET list, GET/PATCH/DELETE /lists/{list_id}/webhooks/{webhook_id}; also configurable per-audience in the web app (Audience > Settings > Webhooks), where update-type checkboxes select trigger events
event_filtering: per-webhook set of event flags (checkbox 'update types' per audience webhook) plus source filters (whether user/admin/API-originated changes fire); webhook is scoped to one list/audience
signature_scheme: X-Mailchimp-Signature: t={unix_ts},v1={hex} where v1 = HMAC-SHA256(signing_secret, "{timestamp}.{raw_body}"); signing secret shown once at creation; verification optional; reject if timestamp older than 5 minutes; deliveries are application/x-www-form-urlencoded
retry_disable_policy: 10-second response timeout; failed deliveries retried at increasing intervals over 75 minutes; excessive or unresponsive webhooks may be dropped or disabled at Mailchimp's discretion
dedup_mechanism: no delivery-id header documented; payload has fired_at timestamp and data.id — consumers dedupe on content
learnings: Mailchimp's timestamped signature format (t={ts},v1={hex} HMAC-SHA256 over 'timestamp.body' with 5-min replay window, Stripe-style) is the exact scheme attune should copy — it is the most modern of the six. Avoid: form-encoded payloads (JSON is table stakes), the short 75-minute retry horizon, discretionary undefined auto-disable, and the missing delivery id. Note its Instant Zapier triggers cover only the subscriber lifecycle where webhooks exist — trigger coverage tracks the webhook vocabulary 1:1.

name: PostHog
zapier_auth: Custom/API-key: 'Personal API Key' field sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>, plus optional API Host field for Cloud EU/self-hosted (from official posthog-zapier repo authentication.ts)
action_examples: Capture Event (org + project + event name + distinct_id + properties dict + timestamp)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/projects/{project_id}/hooks/ with body {target: <url>, event: <event>, resource_id: <action_id>}; DELETE /api/projects/{project_id}/hooks/{hook_id}. Programmatic REST-hook API, but target domain is hard-restricted to hooks.zapier.com and the endpoint is hidden from API docs (hide_api_docs=true). Create internally provisions a HogFunction CDP destination. General-purpose webhooks are dashboard-configured CDP 'HTTP Webhook' destinations instead.
event_filtering: one event string per subscription (HOOK_EVENTS validated at write; only 'action_performed' remains valid) plus resource_id scoping to a specific Action; CDP destinations filter by action/event match rules
signature_scheme: none documented — Zapier hook payload carries no HMAC header; body includes hook.id/hook.event/hook.target envelope
retry_disable_policy: not documented for the hooks API; delivery now runs through CDP HogFunctions (webhook template throws on status >= 400, retries handled by pipeline, no published schedule)
dedup_mechanism: payload envelope hook.id is set to the event UUID (eventUuid also in data) — consumer-side dedup key
learnings: Copy PostHog's REST-hook triad: POST/DELETE hooks endpoint taking {target, event, resource_id} with the subscribe response id used for unsubscribe — it maps 1:1 onto Zapier's performSubscribe/performUnsubscribe. Avoid their Zapier-only target-domain restriction and hidden API docs; attune's endpoint should be public and generic. Also note they validate event against an allow-list at write time, matching attune's append-only source discipline.

name: Amplitude
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — 'Webhooks Streaming' destination created in Amplitude Data > Destinations UI (webhook URL + up to 5 custom headers + event/user forwarding toggles); no public subscription API
event_filtering: per-sync UI event picker ('Select and filter events') on the destination; no event-type string vocabulary — streams selected product analytics events and Identify calls
signature_scheme: none documented — only preset headers Content-Type: application/json and User-Agent: Amplitude/Webhook/1.0, plus user-defined static headers
retry_disable_policy: 1 initial attempt + 9 more over 4 hours on failure; within each attempt an immediate inner retry for 5xx/429: max 3 tries, exponential from 100ms doubling with 50% jitter, capped at 4s
dedup_mechanism: none documented for webhook delivery
learnings: Amplitude's Zapier directory entry is an empty 'upcoming' placeholder (no implementation, zero triggers/actions) — a warning that a directory listing without a real connector is worse than none. Their two-layer retry (outer 10 attempts/4h + inner fast retry with jitter for 5xx/429) is a solid pattern attune can copy. Its FreeMarker payload templating is powerful but heavyweight; attune should prefer a fixed versioned envelope.

name: Mixpanel
zapier_auth: API key ('other'): Project Token field + optional Region field (EU/India data residency) — write-only ingestion token, no OAuth (from Zapier v4 implementations API)
trigger_examples: (only hidden 'Test Auth' polling read exists — no user-facing triggers)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — cohort webhooks via Data > Destinations > Add Destination > Webhook (URL + optional Basic Auth); alert webhooks via Gear > Destinations > Notification Webhook (URL + Basic Auth username/password). Webhook URL cannot even be edited or deleted after creation, only disconnected.
event_filtering: not event-typed — per-cohort sync selection; each POST carries an 'action' field (members/add_members/remove_members) plus parameters.mixpanel_cohort_id; alerts route per-alert to a chosen webhook
signature_scheme: none — optional HTTP Basic Authentication only
retry_disable_policy: cohort syncs every 30 min, batch 1000 users/call; 5 retries over 60s with exponential backoff on 5xx/429; syncs PAUSED (with email notification) on non-transient 400/401/403/404; 3-day snapshot expiry forces full re-sync; expects a JSON ack body {action, status: success|failure, error}
dedup_mechanism: mixpanel_session_id identifies one export, page_info {total_pages, page_count} orders multi-page payloads; docs explicitly warn duplicate member delivery after mid-sync failure — consumer must dedup
learnings: Mixpanel is action-only on Zapier (push data in, no triggers out) — attune should do the opposite and lead with instant triggers. Copy their explicit non-transient-4xx pause + email-notification policy and their response-ack contract idea; avoid their un-editable/un-deletable webhook config and their requirement that receivers implement diff/dedup logic themselves.

name: Heap
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — beta 'Event Webhooks' created in the in-app webhooks console (URL + custom HTTP headers + templated one-level JSON body + triggering events); feature must be enabled by support. Zapier integration is done manually via 'Webhooks by Zapier' Catch Hook on the trigger side and raw POSTs to https://heapanalytics.com/api/track on the action side.
event_filtering: per-webhook list of triggering events chosen from the account's defined/labeled events — no fixed event-type string vocabulary
signature_scheme: none — 'Webhooks only support basic header authentication methods' (static headers); no HMAC documented
retry_disable_policy: not documented; beta explicitly disclaims uptime/deliverability guarantees and reserves the right to shut down webhooks causing load
dedup_mechanism: none documented
learnings: Heap shows the cost of not shipping a first-party connector: its Zapier directory page 404s and users are pointed at generic Webhooks-by-Zapier plumbing with hand-built JSON payloads. Its beta webhook limits (one-level JSON nesting, no arrays, static-header auth only, no retry contract) are all things attune's design should explicitly exceed.

name: Hotjar
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (auth_type: oauth, access_token + refresh_token fields per Zapier v4 implementations API)
trigger_examples: (hidden polling helpers: List Feedback Widgets, List Surveys)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — webhook URL is entered per Survey or per Recording Segment in the Hotjar UI (Scale plan); no public programmatic subscription endpoint documented
event_filtering: one endpoint per resource (survey / recording segment); envelope is {event: <name>, version: 1, data: {...}} and receivers must tolerate unknown event types and unknown fields
signature_scheme: com-hotjar-signature header, HMAC-SHA3-256 over the raw payload bytes with a per-site signing key ('View Webhook key' in settings); payload timestamp used for replay prevention (discard if >5 min old, verify HMAC first)
retry_disable_policy: up to 6 retries: 30s, 1m, 2m, 5m, 10m, 20m; stops on any 2xx; HTTP 410 response causes Hotjar to DELETE the webhook; HTTPS required; 10s response timeout
dedup_mechanism: explicit requirement: receivers dedup on the unique identifier in each message (e.g. survey response id / api_id); duplicates possible
learnings: Hotjar is the best single model for attune's webhook contract: versioned envelope {event, version, data}, snake_case event names, documented retry ladder with 410-based auto-unsubscribe, HMAC signature header + timestamp replay protection, and explicit forward-compatibility rules (tolerate unknown events/fields). Copy nearly all of it — but use HMAC-SHA256 rather than SHA3-256 for ecosystem tooling compatibility, and expose subscriptions via API, not just dashboard. Their all-Instant, zero-action Zapier app also validates a trigger-first connector.

name: Segment
zapier_auth: API key ('other'): Segment Public API token (Workspace Settings > Access Management > Tokens) + required Region field (api.segmentapis.com vs eu1.api.segmentapis.com); listed as a Premium Zapier app under slug twilio-segment
trigger_examples: New Event (Instant — fires when an event reaches a 'Zapier Actions' destination; inputs: destinationId, zapIdentifier, fqlType/custom FQL filter, sampleEvent)
(hidden polling helpers: List Destinations, List Sources)
webhook_sub_endpoint: hybrid: classic Webhooks destination is dashboard-configured (up to 5 URLs + headers + sharedSecret); the Zapier app provisions 'Zapier Actions' destinations programmatically through the Segment Public API (api.segmentapis.com) with per-subscription FQL filters — general destination/subscription CRUD is available via that Public API
event_filtering: spec-type based (the 7 Segment spec call types) plus per-subscription FQL (Filter Query Language) predicates for fine-grained event matching in Actions destinations
signature_scheme: X-Signature header, hex HMAC-SHA1 of the JSON-stringified request body using the configured sharedSecret; for batched delivery only the FIRST event in the batch is signed
retry_disable_policy: 5s response timeout; retries temporary failures (timeouts, 5xx) for up to 4 hours; with multiple webhook URLs, success on any one URL stops retries to the others
dedup_mechanism: none documented in the webhook destination docs (no delivery-id header)
learnings: Segment's FQL-per-subscription filtering is the power-user ceiling for event filtering — attune only needs the simpler event-type-array model, but should note the pattern of the Zapier trigger programmatically creating a scoped subscription (destinationId + zapIdentifier) per Zap. Avoid HMAC-SHA1 and the sign-only-first-event-in-batch quirk, which is confusing and weak; sign the whole body with SHA-256.
sources: https://zapier.com/apps/twilio-segment/integrations (NEXT_DATA JSON incl. newEvent trigger needs + FQL help text)

name: Customer.io
zapier_auth: API key — Track API credentials (Site ID + API Key) from workspace Account Settings > API Credentials
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /v1/reporting_webhooks (App API, full CRUD: GET list, GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/reporting_webhooks/{webhook_id}); body {name, endpoint, events[], disabled, full_resolution, with_content}
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (enum of flattened object_metric tokens); payload itself carries object_type + metric split (e.g. object_type=email, metric=sent)
signature_scheme: x-cio-signature header: HMAC-SHA256 over the string v0:<x-cio-timestamp>:<body> using a per-webhook signing key; x-cio-timestamp header carries unix timestamp (replay protection)
retry_disable_policy: Expects 2xx within 4 seconds; failed/timed-out calls retried with exponential backoff over 7 days; certain error codes wait 1 hour before retry; subsequent webhook calls are backlogged (ordered delivery) until the failed call succeeds
dedup_mechanism: event_id field (ULID-style) in every event payload
learnings: Copy the flattened <object>_<metric> event token enum plus a structured object_type/metric split in the payload, and the v0:<timestamp>:<body> signing string for replay protection. Note the gap: despite a full programmatic subscription API, Customer.io's Zapier app ships ZERO triggers (outbound events aren't wired to Zapier) — attune should make its webhook-subscription API the backing store for instant Zapier triggers from day one. The 7-day ordered-backlog retry is generous but head-of-line blocking is a tradeoff to weigh against attune's outbox model.

name: Klaviyo
trigger_examples: Profile added to Segment or List (Polling)
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (scopes incl. accounts:read metrics:read events:read/write profiles:read/write lists:read/write subscriptions:read/write campaigns:read/write tags:read/write)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/webhooks (JSON:API; attributes {name, description, endpoint_url, secret_key}, relationships webhook-topics data:[{type:"webhook-topic", id:"event:klaviyo.sent_sms"}]); full CRUD plus topic discovery via GET /api/webhook-topics
event_filtering: per-subscription topic array (JSON:API relationships to webhook-topic resources); topics are dynamic per account based on available metrics, discoverable via GET /api/webhook-topics
signature_scheme: Klaviyo-Signature header: HMAC-SHA256 of request body using a user-supplied secret_key (min 16 chars, required at subscription creation); plus Klaviyo-Webhook-Id and Klaviyo-Timestamp headers
retry_disable_policy: Expects 200/201/202 within 5 seconds; exponential backoff retries with max delay 1 hour; if webhook stays in error state >48 hours it is disabled (enabled flag set to false); one failure never disables
dedup_mechanism: Payload data array items carry external_id (the event's ID); Klaviyo-Webhook-Id header identifies the webhook (not the delivery)
learnings: Copy the discoverable topic catalog endpoint (GET /api/webhook-topics) — it lets a Zapier REST-hook trigger populate a dynamic event dropdown without hardcoding, which suits attune's registry-driven source vocabulary. The subscriber-supplied secret_key (min 16 chars, matching attune's existing webhook-secret rule) and the 48h-error-state auto-disable with enabled=false are clean patterns. Avoid Klaviyo's gap: its Zapier triggers are still polling despite having a webhooks API.

name: ActiveCampaign
trigger_examples: Tag Added or Removed From Contact (Instant)
zapier_auth: API key + account-specific API URL (entered on Connect an Account page)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/3/webhooks with {webhook:{name, url, events[], sources[], listid?, headers[]}}; full CRUD plus GET /api/3/webhook/events to list the event vocabulary
event_filtering: per-subscription events array plus an orthogonal sources array (public/admin/api/system) filtering by who triggered the action; optional listid scoping
signature_scheme: No default signature. Optional custom webhook headers: a header with is_signature=true uses its value as an HMAC-SHA256 secret over the request body and sends the computed signature as that header's value
retry_disable_policy: Webhooks are never retried; delivery is at-least-once and docs explicitly tell consumers to build an idempotent system
dedup_mechanism: None built-in; docs warn events may arrive more than once and require consumer-side idempotency
learnings: Proof that a simple flat snake_case event list + per-subscription events array scales to the largest instant-trigger surface in this batch (22 REST-hook Zapier triggers). The sources[] dimension (who caused the event: public/admin/api/system) is a cheap, useful second filter axis attune could map to its ingest source vocabulary. Avoid: 'never retried' delivery and signature-off-by-default are anti-patterns; attune's outbox retry plus mandatory HMAC should stay.

name: Attio
zapier_auth: API key (workspace access token with scopes; Attio recommends Read-write scopes for Zapier)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /v2/webhooks with {data:{target_url, subscriptions:[{event_type, filter:{$or:[{field,operator,value}]}}]}}; CRUD via /v2/webhooks/{webhook_id}; secret returned in create response
event_filtering: one subscription resource carries an array of {event_type, filter} pairs — event-type array plus optional per-event attribute-level filter expressions ($or of field/operator/value)
signature_scheme: Attio-Signature header (duplicated as X-Attio-Signature for legacy middleware): HMAC-SHA256 of request body using the per-webhook secret
retry_disable_policy: 2xx (e.g. 200/202) = success; otherwise up to 10 retries with exponential backoff over ~3 days, then webhook marked degraded and owner emailed
dedup_mechanism: Idempotency-Key header, unique per message but stable across retries and redeliveries; at-least-once delivery guaranteed
learnings: The cleanest model in this batch and the closest template for attune: noun.verb event types, one webhook carrying an array of {event_type, filter} subscriptions with attribute-level filter expressions, per-webhook secret + HMAC-SHA256 signature header, and an Idempotency-Key delivery header. Its Zapier app is 100% instant triggers built directly on this API. Copy the degraded-state + owner-notification lifecycle instead of silent disablement.

name: Typeform
action_examples: Update Dropdown, Multiple Choice or Ranking Question Options
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (scopes: forms:read forms:write webhooks:read webhooks:write responses:read accounts:read workspaces:read offline)
webhook_sub_endpoint: PUT https://api.typeform.com/forms/{form_id}/webhooks/{tag} — idempotent create-or-update keyed by caller-chosen tag, per form; body {enabled, event_types:{form_response_partial:true}, url, secret, verify_ssl}
event_filtering: scoped per form (path param) + caller-chosen tag; event_types object with boolean flags — tiny fixed vocabulary rather than an event catalog
signature_scheme: Typeform-Signature header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw payload keyed with the webhook secret, base64-encoded, prefixed with sha256=
retry_disable_policy: 30s response timeout; 410 Gone or 404 → no retry, webhook disabled immediately; 429/408/503/423 → retry every 2-3 min for 10 hours; other codes → 5 retries with backoff at 5min/10min/20min/1h/2h/3h/4h; auto-disable + notification if 100% failure within 24h (>300 attempts) or within 5 min (100 attempts)
dedup_mechanism: event_id field in every payload (alongside event_type)
learnings: The PUT-by-tag idempotent upsert is ideal for connector-managed subscriptions — Zapier's subscribeHook can safely re-run without duplicating webhooks; attune should offer an equivalent idempotency handle (client-supplied key or PUT semantics). Also copy the HTTP-status-differentiated retry classes and 410-Gone-means-unsubscribe convention. Avoid the resource-scoped-only filtering (per-form endpoint, 2 event types) — attune needs a real event catalog.

name: SurveyMonkey
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (help article: 'Grant Zapier permission to access your account'; API uses Bearer access tokens)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /v3/webhooks with {name, subscription_url, authorization?, verify_ssl, event_type, object_type, object_ids[]} — one event_type per webhook, scoped to specific surveys/collectors
event_filtering: single event_type per subscription (not an array) + object_type/object_ids resource scoping — multiple events require multiple webhooks
signature_scheme: Sm-Signature header: HMAC-SHA1 of the raw body keyed with '<client_id>&<client_secret>' (base64); Sm-Apikey header also sent; Content-Type application/vnd.surveymonkey.<object>.v1+json
learnings: Copy the object_type/object_ids resource-scoping idea (a subscription bound to specific surveys maps well to attune scoping a subscription to specific tenants/sources), and the vendor-namespaced Content-Type for payload versioning. Avoid the single-event_type-per-webhook design (forces N webhooks for N events; every other product in this batch uses an events array) and the legacy HMAC-SHA1 keyed with app credentials instead of a per-webhook secret. Retry/auto-disable policy is not documented in the v3 API docs — an underspecified contract attune should not repeat.

name: Square
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Square and grant Zapier permission)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /v2/webhooks/subscriptions with body { idempotency_key, subscription: { name, event_types: [...], notification_url, api_version } }; returns server-generated signature_key. Full CRUD: list/retrieve/update/delete subscriptions, update signature key, test subscription, plus GET list-webhook-event-types.
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (event_types field); multiple subscriptions per app allowed
signature_scheme: x-square-hmacsha256-signature header; HMAC-SHA256 over (notification URL + raw request body) keyed with the subscription's signature_key
retry_disable_policy: Retries with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours after the originating event; after 24h the notification is discarded. No documented auto-disable.
dedup_mechanism: event_id field in each notification body is the documented idempotency value (webhooks 'can be sent more than once'); create-subscription call itself takes an idempotency_key
