learnings: Square is the cleanest reference for attune's public subscription API: a first-class /v2/webhooks/subscriptions resource with an event_types array, a server-generated per-subscription signature_key (rotatable via a dedicated endpoint), a test-delivery endpoint, and a list-event-types discovery endpoint. Notably its Zapier app still uses polling triggers, showing the Zapier surface and the webhook API are independent decisions. Copy the discovery + test + key-rotation endpoints; include URL in the HMAC input only if you accept the extra coupling (body-only HMAC like Notion is simpler).
sources: https://help.zapier.com (How to get started with Square on Zapier)

name: Chargebee
zapier_auth: API key + site name (form fields: Site Name and API Key)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only (Settings > Configure Chargebee > API Keys and Webhooks > Webhooks tab; up to 5 webhooks per site). Events are also retrievable by polling GET https://[site].chargebee.com/api/v2/events.
event_filtering: per-webhook 'Events to Send' dropdown selection (all events by default, can narrow to a chosen set); max 5 webhook endpoints per site
signature_scheme: No HMAC signature. Security options are HTTP Basic Auth on the webhook URL or a random secret key embedded in the URL path; docs suggest re-fetching the event via Retrieve an Event API to verify integrity.
retry_disable_policy: Fixed retry schedule, up to 7 retries: 2min, +6min, +30min, +1h, +5h, +1d, +2d (last retry ~3 days 7 hours after event). Webhooks can be manually deactivated; unused test-site webhooks prompt email nagging.
dedup_mechanism: Unique event id field in payload (docs prescribe storing processed ids for the 3d7h retry window); out-of-order delivery handled via resource_version millisecond timestamp on resources
learnings: Chargebee shows how far you can get with an all-Instant Zapier app (all 17 visible triggers are REST-hook Instant) even when the underlying config is dashboard-only — but attune should avoid its two weakest choices: no HMAC signature (basic-auth-or-secret-URL is below current bar) and a hard 5-endpoint cap. Its snake_case resource_verb vocabulary and the documented store-event-id-for-the-retry-window dedup recipe are worth citing.

name: Calendly
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Calendly, grant Zapier permission)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.calendly.com/webhook_subscriptions with body { url, events: [...], organization, scope: "organization"|"user", user?, signing_key? }; GET list (filter by organization/scope/user), GET/DELETE /webhook_subscriptions/{uuid}. Response resource includes callback_url, events[], state, retry_started_at.
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (events field) plus a scope dimension (organization vs user, with org/user URIs in the body)
signature_scheme: Calendly-Webhook-Signature header, format t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex>; HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw-body>" keyed with the caller-supplied signing_key (Stripe-style, replay-protected)
retry_disable_policy: Subscription resource exposes state and retry_started_at fields indicating a retrying/failed state; exact backoff schedule not found in retrieved sources
dedup_mechanism: No dedicated delivery-id header found in retrieved sources; payload carries created_at and resource URIs
learnings: Calendly is the closest shape to what attune needs: a small CRUD /webhook_subscriptions resource where the caller supplies both the events array and the signing_key, enabling fully self-service REST hooks (n8n/activepieces/Zapier all drive it programmatically). Copy the caller-supplied-secret + t=,v1= timestamped HMAC (replay protection built in) and the scope dimension (maps to attune's tenant scoping); note its tiny 3-event vocabulary kept the Zapier trigger list almost 1:1 with webhook events.
sources: https://help.zapier.com (How to get started with Calendly on Zapier)

name: Slack
trigger_examples: New Reaction Added in a Channel
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Slack, grant workspace permission; scope-gated)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only per app: one Events API Request URL configured in app settings (or app manifest), with an event subscription list tied to the app's granted OAuth scopes; URL verified via url_verification challenge. No public per-customer REST subscription endpoint.
event_filtering: per-app event-subscription list bound to OAuth scopes ('Subscribe to only the events you want'); all subscribed events for all installs flow to the single app endpoint
signature_scheme: X-Slack-Signature header, value v0=<hex> = HMAC-SHA256 of "v0:<X-Slack-Request-Timestamp>:<raw body>" keyed with the app signing secret; timestamp checked to block replays
retry_disable_policy: Must respond HTTP 2xx within 3 seconds; on failure retries 3 times with increasing gaps (~immediate, 1 min, 5 min) carrying x-slack-retry-num and x-slack-retry-reason headers; app event delivery is temporarily disabled if success rate falls below 5% per 60 minutes (apps under 1,000 events/hour exempt)
dedup_mechanism: event_id (e.g. Ev123ABC456) + event_time in the outer envelope; x-slack-retry-num header identifies redelivery attempts
learnings: Slack's model (one app-level endpoint, events bound to OAuth scopes) doesn't fit attune's per-tenant subscriptions, but three operational details are worth copying: the 3-second-ack + retry-reason header contract, the explicit success-rate-based auto-disable rule with a small-sender exemption, and the versioned v0= signature prefix that leaves room for algorithm rotation. Its mixed event naming (message.channels dotted subtype vs reaction_added snake_case) is an anti-pattern — attune should pick one style.
sources: https://help.zapier.com (How to get started with Slack on Zapier)

name: Discord
zapier_auth: OAuth2 with bot install (scopes: bot identify; requires server Manage Webhooks permission)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only: one Webhook Events URL per app configured on the developer-portal Webhooks page; endpoint must ack a PING (type 0) with 204 before it is accepted. (Chat activity events like messages are not on this surface at all — they require a Gateway websocket bot, which is what Zapier's app uses.)
event_filtering: per-app checklist of webhook event types enabled on the single endpoint (subscribe on the same settings page)
signature_scheme: X-Signature-Ed25519 + X-Signature-Timestamp headers; Ed25519 public-key signature over timestamp+body (not HMAC); invalid signatures must get a 401
retry_disable_policy: Respond 204 (empty body) within 3 seconds; failures retried with exponential backoff for up to 10 minutes; Discord runs automated security probes (deliberately invalid signatures) and removes your Webhook Events URL + emails you if validation fails
dedup_mechanism: No documented delivery-id/dedup header on webhook events in retrieved sources; envelope has version (always 1), type, and timestamp
learnings: Discord splits real-time into Gateway (websocket, chat activity) vs webhook events (small lifecycle vocabulary), which is why its Zapier triggers are bot/polling-based with zero Instant labels — a warning that if attune's webhook vocabulary is too narrow, integrators fall back to polling. Its asymmetric Ed25519 signing (no shared secret to leak) and proactive invalid-signature probing are interesting hardening ideas, but HMAC remains the ecosystem default Zapier-style consumers expect; the 10-minute retry window is notably short.
sources: https://help.zapier.com (How to get started with Discord on Zapier)

name: Notion
trigger_examples: Updated Content in Data Source Item
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (log into Notion, grant page/workspace access to Zapier)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only: created in the integration's connection settings (Webhooks tab > + Create a subscription: enter HTTPS URL, pick event types). Verified via a one-time POST containing a verification_token that must be echoed back to activate.
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type checklist chosen at creation (modifiable later); events also implicitly scoped to pages/databases the connection can access
signature_scheme: X-Notion-Signature header, value sha256=<hex>; HMAC-SHA256 of the request body keyed with the subscription's verification_token
retry_disable_policy: Aims for at-most-once delivery; on failed acknowledgment retries up to 8 times with exponential backoff, final attempt ~24 hours after the initial event
dedup_mechanism: Top-level event id (UUID) + subscription_id + attempt_number (1-8) in every payload; related rapid edits are aggregated/debounced into single events (~1 min)
learnings: Notion has the vocabulary attune should imitate: strict entity.verb_past_tense strings (page.created, comment.deleted) with a payload envelope carrying id, timestamp, subscription_id, entity and attempt_number — attempt_number in-band is a cheap, copyable dedup/observability win, as is event aggregation to debounce edit storms. Its verification_token handshake doubles as the HMAC key, one less secret to manage; but being dashboard-only means Zapier still gets Instant triggers while third parties can't self-serve — attune's differentiator should be Calendly/Square-style programmatic subscription with this vocabulary style.
sources: https://help.zapier.com (How to get started with Notion on Zapier)

name: GitHub
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Zapier's SDK panel on the app page says 'Zapier handles the OAuth and scoped permissions'; app-specific auth doc not retrievable, so scheme inferred rather than directly confirmed)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks with body {config:{url, secret, insecure_ssl}, events: array of strings (default ["push"]), active: bool}; fully programmatic plus dashboard UI; also org- and app-level hooks
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array (`events` array of strings per hook); fine-grained action (opened/closed/edited) is NOT filterable at subscription time — it arrives in the payload `action` field and receivers filter client-side
signature_scheme: X-Hub-Signature-256: HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of raw body with shared secret, value prefixed 'sha256='; legacy X-Hub-Signature (HMAC-SHA1) kept for compatibility
retry_disable_policy: GitHub does NOT automatically redeliver failed deliveries; delivery marked failed if no 2xx within 10 seconds; consumers must poll the deliveries REST API and redeliver manually/scripted
dedup_mechanism: X-GitHub-Delivery header (globally unique GUID per event, stable across redeliveries); plus X-GitHub-Event (event name) and X-GitHub-Hook-ID headers
learnings: Copy: the resource-noun events array + payload-level `action` sub-field is the cleanest two-tier vocabulary, and the delivery-GUID header + list-deliveries/redeliver API is the gold standard for consumer-side recovery. Avoid: GitHub's own Zapier app is 100% polling (0 Instant triggers, 24 read keys in the implementation) — proof that without a lightweight programmatic per-URL subscribe API (REST-hook style), even a webhook-rich platform ends up polling in Zapier; attune should design its subscription endpoint so Zapier can create/delete hooks per Zap. Note GitHub also ships no automatic retry, which pushes recovery cost onto every consumer — attune should do better.

name: GitLab
zapier_auth: Unconfirmed from retrieved sources (GitLab's own zapier.md doc 403'd/moved; directory page shows no auth text). GitLab API supports PAT and OAuth2; scheme not verified
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /projects/:id/hooks with {url required, per-event boolean flags (push_events, issues_events, merge_requests_events, note_events, job_events, pipeline_events, ...), branch_filter_strategy (wildcard|regex|all_branches), custom_headers, custom_webhook_template, signing_token, enable_ssl_verification}; also group hooks; fully programmatic + dashboard
event_filtering: per-subscription boolean flag per event class (not an array) + branch filter for push; payload carries object_kind + action (open/update/merge)
signature_scheme: Standard Webhooks spec: webhook-signature header 'v1,{base64_signature}' = HMAC-SHA256 over '{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}' when a signing token is set (GitLab 19.0+); legacy X-Gitlab-Token plain-text secret header
retry_disable_policy: Auto-disable: webhook temporarily disabled after 4 consecutive failures, permanently disabled after 40 consecutive failures (17.11+); per-event resend API POST /projects/:id/hooks/:hook_id/events/:hook_event_id/resend (rate-limited 5/min); guidance: return 4xx only for misconfiguration, avoid 5xx
dedup_mechanism: webhook-id header (Standard Webhooks message id, stable across redelivery) + X-Gitlab-Event-UUID (unique per non-recursive event) + Idempotency-Key on resends
learnings: Copy: GitLab is the best modern reference — it adopted the Standard Webhooks spec (webhook-id/webhook-timestamp/webhook-signature v1,base64 HMAC-SHA256 over id.timestamp.body), which attune should adopt verbatim for interop; its 4-strikes-temporary / 40-strikes-permanent auto-disable ladder and per-event resend API are concrete, testable policies. Its 9 Instant Zapier triggers (vs GitHub's 0) show programmatic project-scoped hooks map directly to REST-hook triggers. Avoid: the boolean-flag-per-event-class subscription shape — it can't grow without schema changes; an events array scales better.

name: Sentry
webhook_sub_endpoint: Two paths: (1) Integration Platform (current): webhook URL + resource subscriptions configured on an Internal/Public Integration in the dashboard (dashboard-config, not per-URL API); (2) legacy Service Hooks API: POST /api/0/projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/hooks/ with body {url: string required, events: array(string) required} — requires 'servicehooks' feature flag and bearer token with project:write scope
event_filtering: per-integration resource-type subscription (checkbox per resource: issue, error, comment, ...); resource arrives in Sentry-Hook-Resource header, verb in payload `action` field; legacy service hooks use an events array
signature_scheme: Sentry-Hook-Signature: HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the JSON body keyed by the integration's Client Secret; plus Request-ID and Sentry-Hook-Timestamp headers
dedup_mechanism: Request-ID header (unique identifier for tracking specific events)
learnings: Notable: Sentry has NO official Zapier app (zapier.com/apps/sentry 404s; directory search returns only unrelated 'SentryKit'/'PassEntry') despite a mature webhook platform — a gap attune can exploit by shipping a first-class Zapier connector early. Copy: the resource-in-header (Sentry-Hook-Resource) + action-in-payload split makes routing cheap without parsing the body. Avoid: gating programmatic webhook creation behind a feature flag ('servicehooks') and splitting webhooks across two half-generations (service hooks vs integration platform) — confusing for integrators.

name: PagerDuty
zapier_auth: Unconfirmed from retrieved sources (support.pagerduty.com/docs/zapier now 404; directory page carries no auth text). PagerDuty REST API supports API token and OAuth2 (scoped); scheme not verified
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /webhook_subscriptions with {webhook_subscription: {delivery_method: {type: 'http_delivery_method', url, custom_headers}, events: array(string) min 1 unique, filter: {type: service_reference|team_reference|account_reference, id}, description, active}}; secret returned only on create response; scoped OAuth webhook_subscriptions.write; plus /enable and /ping sub-endpoints
event_filtering: per-subscription event-type array + a scoping filter object (service/team/account reference)
signature_scheme: X-PagerDuty-Signature: comma-separated list of 'v1='-prefixed HMAC-SHA256 hex digests of the raw body (multiple signatures support zero-downtime secret rotation); mutual TLS and OAuth-bearer delivery also offered
retry_disable_policy: Retries on timeout/5xx/429/connection failures, periodically for up to 48h (drops after); permanent drop on other 4xx; after 3 consecutive dropped webhooks the subscription is disabled for 24h (temporarily_disabled=true) and queued deliveries dropped; re-enable via UI or the enable API; 2xx expected within 5s (16s for custom incident actions)
dedup_mechanism: X-Webhook-Id header — unique per webhook event, repeated on every retry attempt; explicit at-least-once delivery contract with in-order delivery per subscription up to 55KB
learnings: Copy: PagerDuty v3 is the strongest overall template for attune's subscription API — single POST resource with url + events[] + scope filter, secret returned exactly once, versioned comma-separated multi-signature header for rotation, documented 48h retry window, 3-strikes/24h temp-disable, ping endpoint, and a stable X-Webhook-Id for dedup under at-least-once semantics. Its noun.verb(.subnoun) event names (incident.responder.added) are a good naming model. Note: even with all this, its Zapier surface is thin (1 instant trigger) — a small connector over a good API is fine.

name: Datadog
zapier_auth: Unconfirmed from retrieved sources; Datadog API generally authenticates with API key + application key, but the Zapier connection doc was not retrievable
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /api/v1/integration/webhooks/configuration/webhooks with {name required, url required, payload (custom template, nullable), custom_headers (JSON string, nullable), encode_as: json|form} — creates a NAMED webhook, not an event subscription; delivery is wired by mentioning @webhook-<WEBHOOK_NAME> in a monitor's notification message
event_filtering: no per-subscription event array — routing is per-monitor via @webhook-NAME mentions in alert messages; payload is a user-defined template with $VARIABLES ($EVENT_TYPE, $ALERT_ID, $HOSTNAME, ...)
signature_scheme: none documented — no signature header; integrators are expected to use custom headers (e.g. their own auth token) or URL auth
retry_disable_policy: Retries only on Datadog-internal error or 5xx from the endpoint; 15-second per-request timeout; missed connections retried 5 times; no documented auto-disable
dedup_mechanism: no dedicated delivery-id header documented; $ID / $ALERT_ID template variables in the payload are the only correlation handles
learnings: Avoid: the notification-template model (@webhook-NAME mentions + user-defined payload template, no event subscription array, no signature, no delivery id) makes machine-consumable integrations fragile — its Zapier app is nearly empty (0 visible triggers, 2 actions) as a direct consequence. Copy: nothing structural, though the $VARIABLE payload templating is a nice power-user escape hatch attune could offer as an optional overlay on a fixed canonical payload, similar to GitLab's custom_webhook_template.

name: Opsgenie
zapier_auth: API key — Opsgenie's own doc: create a Zapier integration under Settings > Integrations, copy the API Key, and 'Paste your Opsgenie API Key into the "API Key field"' in Zapier
webhook_sub_endpoint: Dashboard-first: Webhook added via Settings > Integrations UI with per-alert-action 'post to URL' mappings; integrations are also manageable programmatically via POST https://api.opsgenie.com/v2/integrations (GenieKey auth) with alert filters {conditionMatchType, conditions[]}, but there is no simple url+events[] subscription resource
event_filtering: per-integration mapping of alert actions to the webhook URL (if alert is created -> post to URL), plus tag/custom-action qualifiers and condition filters; not an event-type array
signature_scheme: none documented in retrieved docs — payload includes integrationId/integrationName; custom headers supported for receiver-side auth
dedup_mechanism: no delivery-id header documented; payload carries alertId and integrationId for correlation
learnings: Avoid: PascalCase bare-verb action vocabulary (Create, AddNote, Close) without a resource prefix — it collides as soon as a second resource type exists; attune should namespace as resource.verb. Also avoid dashboard-only subscription config with no signature and no documented retry contract: Opsgenie's Zapier app shrank to a single Create Alert action (inbound only), showing that without a clean outbound subscription API the ecosystem integration stays one-directional. Note Opsgenie is being sunset into Atlassian JSM, so weight its patterns accordingly.

name: Airtable
zapier_auth: OAuth2 (Zapier migrated the app from Airtable API keys to OAuth — help article 'Latest update on migrating from Airtable API Keys to OAuth')
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST /v0/bases/{baseId}/webhooks with body {notificationUrl, specification:{options:{filters:{dataTypes:[...], changeTypes:[add|remove|update], recordChangeScope}}}} — returns {id, macSecretBase64, expirationTime}; plus refresh (POST .../webhooks/{webhookId}/refresh), delete, enable/disable notifications, and GET list-webhook-payloads (cursor-based)
event_filtering: per-subscription filter object (dataTypes + changeTypes arrays + recordChangeScope), not flat event-name strings; docs strongly recommend specifying filters
signature_scheme: X-Airtable-Content-MAC header, value 'hmac-sha256=' + hex HMAC-SHA256 of raw body keyed with base64-decoded macSecretBase64 (secret returned only once at creation)
retry_disable_policy: Webhooks created with OAuth/PAT expire and are disabled after 7 days unless refreshed (refresh-a-webhook or list-webhook-payloads extends life); metadata+payloads readable 7 more days after expiry; limits: 10 webhooks/base, 2 per OAuth integration per base; ping-level retry schedule not documented
dedup_mechanism: thin notification ping + client pulls payloads via list-webhook-payloads with a monotonically increasing cursor (cursorForNextPayload); client tracks cursor so deliveries are exactly-ordered and deduplicated by design
learnings: Airtable's ping-then-pull model (thin notification, cursor-based payload fetch) gives exactly-once ordering without idempotency headers, but it forces expiry/refresh ceremony (7-day TTL) that Zapier's REST-hook model can't use — notably Airtable's own Zapier triggers are still polling despite having a webhooks API. attune should prefer fat payloads with per-subscription event arrays so Zapier Instant triggers work, but copy the one-time-secret-at-creation pattern (macSecretBase64) and explicit filter object.

name: Cal.com
zapier_auth: API key (Cal.com-generated Zapier API key; Cal.com's legacy Zapier subscription endpoints accept both API key and OAuth per repo README)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.cal.com/v2/webhooks with body {active, subscriberUrl, triggers:[...], payloadTemplate, secret, version}; also GET/PATCH/DELETE /v2/webhooks; Zapier app uses dedicated POST /api/integrations/zapier/addSubscription + DELETE .../deleteSubscription (REST-hook pattern)
event_filtering: per-subscription array of trigger event types (triggers:[...]); webhooks can be scoped to user, event-type, or team level
signature_scheme: x-cal-signature-256 header, HMAC-SHA256 hex of the raw payload using the per-webhook secret (secret optional); payload version in x-cal-webhook-version header (e.g. 2021-10-20)
retry_disable_policy: General retry/auto-disable policy not documented; delegation-credential webhooks documented as retried on transient network errors and HTTP 408/429/5xx; subscriber URL validated at creation (SaaS: HTTPS only, private IPs/localhost/metadata endpoints blocked)
dedup_mechanism: idempotencyKey field present in MEETING_STARTED/MEETING_ENDED payloads; no delivery-id header documented for other events
learnings: Cal.com is the cleanest OSS reference for attune: a programmatic subscription endpoint (url + triggers array + optional secret), SCREAMING_SNAKE event vocabulary, x-cal-signature-256 HMAC-SHA256, payload versioning via header, and a dedicated thin addSubscription/deleteSubscription pair that powers 100%-Instant Zapier triggers. Copy the subscriber-URL SSRF validation (HTTPS-only, block private IPs) and the version header; avoid their gap of an undocumented retry/disable policy.

name: Ghost
zapier_auth: API key / custom auth — Admin API URL + Admin API Key from Ghost Admin's built-in Zapier integration (TryGhost/Zapier CLI app, field key adminApiKey)
webhook_sub_endpoint: Admin UI (Settings > Advanced > Integrations > Add custom integration: one trigger event + target URL) or Admin API /webhooks/ resource (Add/Edit/Delete, stable) — one event per webhook, no events array
event_filtering: one event per webhook registration (create N webhooks for N events); noun.verb and noun.verb.qualifier naming
signature_scheme: X-Ghost-Signature header: 'sha256={HMAC-SHA256-hex of payload+timestamp}, t={timestamp}' using the integration secret (from webhook-trigger.js source)
retry_disable_policy: 2xx = success; up to 5 retries per delivery (got library retry limit 5, 2s request timeout); an HTTP 410 response destroys the webhook automatically; failures recorded as last_triggered_status/last_triggered_error
dedup_mechanism: none documented — no delivery-id header or event id in the envelope
learnings: Ghost proves a small, fully-Instant Zapier surface (10 hook triggers, 5 actions) works fine on a one-event-per-webhook model, but that model multiplies registrations — attune's events-array-per-subscription is strictly better. Worth copying: HTTP 410 as a subscriber-initiated auto-unsubscribe signal, and embedding the signing timestamp inside the signature header (sha256=..., t=...) to prevent replay. Avoid: no delivery-id means consumers cannot dedup retried deliveries.

name: Supabase
zapier_auth: no official app — Supabase's own partner guide routes users through Zapier's generic PostgreSQL app using a dedicated least-privilege 'zapier' Postgres user (database credentials)
trigger_examples: New Row (via generic PostgreSQL app, polling, 50 most-recent-rows limit)
Custom Query (via generic PostgreSQL app, polling)
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only or raw SQL — Database Webhooks are pg_net trigger wrappers: CREATE TRIGGER ... AFTER INSERT ON table EXECUTE FUNCTION supabase_functions.http_request(url, method, headers, params, timeout_ms); no REST subscription endpoint with url+events array
event_filtering: per-trigger table + event selection (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE checkboxes per table); payload carries {type, table, schema, record, old_record}
signature_scheme: none documented — headers are caller-configurable in http_request but no built-in HMAC signing
retry_disable_policy: not documented — pg_net is async fire-and-forget with a per-request timeout; no retry schedule or auto-disable policy in docs
dedup_mechanism: none documented
learnings: Supabase shows the cost of NOT having an event-subscription product: users fall back to Zapier's generic PostgreSQL polling app (50-row window, missed events) and Supabase's docs must apologize for it. Database Webhooks (pg_net) are a low-level primitive without signing, retries, or dedup — attune should not model its public webhook API on raw DB triggers; a first-class subscription resource with signing and retries is the differentiator.
sources: https://supabase.com/partners/catalog/zapier (RSC payload: PostgreSQL-app guide, 'zapier' PG user, New Row/Custom Query, 50-row limitation)

name: Plausible
event_filtering: unknown — no outbound webhook feature exists; docs offer only Stats API / Events API / Sites API (inbound + read), email reports, traffic spike/drop email alerts, and Slack reports
learnings: Plausible has no Zapier app and no outbound webhook/subscription API at all — its notification story is email + Slack reports only, and its public APIs (Stats/Events/Sites) are pull-style. For attune this is the anti-benchmark: an analytics-adjacent OSS product with no event-push surface cannot participate in automation ecosystems; even a minimal subscription API would have unlocked a Zapier listing.
sources: https://plausible.io/docs (full docs nav: no webhooks page)
GitHub code search plausible/analytics: no zapier/webhook-subscription code paths

name: Novu
webhook_sub_endpoint: dashboard-only — endpoints are added in the Novu dashboard Webhooks page (URL + description + selected event types + advanced config); no public REST endpoint for outbound webhook subscriptions is documented (the 'auto-configure integration for inbound webhooks' API endpoint is for inbound provider webhooks, not subscriptions)
event_filtering: per-endpoint event-type selection at configuration time (choose specific event types per endpoint); noun.verb lowercase naming
signature_scheme: Svix-style: webhook-id + webhook-timestamp + webhook-signature headers, signature 'v1,{base64 HMAC-SHA256}' verified with the svix library against the raw body
retry_disable_policy: exponential backoff schedule: immediately, 5s, 5m, 30m, 2h, 5h, 10h, 10h; 15s response timeout; endpoint auto-disabled after all attempts fail for 5 days (manual re-enable); manual retry, bulk 'Recover Failed Messages' since a timestamp, and per-message Replay
dedup_mechanism: webhook-id header (unique message id, stable across retries) — standard Svix delivery-id semantics
learnings: Novu outsources webhook delivery to Svix and gets an excellent operational story for free: documented backoff schedule, 5-day auto-disable with manual re-enable, replay/recovery windows, and the webhook-id/timestamp/signature header triple that consumers can dedup on. attune should adopt this exact envelope contract (delivery-id header stable across retries + timestamped HMAC) and Novu's published retry schedule; note that even with great webhooks Novu still has no Zapier listing — a connector requires the Zapier-side app work too.

name: Qualtrics
zapier_auth: Not stated in directory or a help article; the Qualtrics platform API itself authenticates via X-API-TOKEN header (API key) or OAuth 2.0, so the Zapier app most plausibly collects an API token + data center, but this was not directly confirmed
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://{dc}.qualtrics.com/API/v3/eventsubscriptions with JSON {publicationUrl, topics, encrypt, sharedKey}; GET /eventsubscriptions (list), GET/DELETE /eventsubscriptions/{id}; requires brand administrator
event_filtering: single topics STRING per subscription (not an array) — one event, optionally suffixed by resource ID, or wildcard star notation (threesixty.*); one subscription = one topic pattern
signature_scheme: No signature header; optional sharedKey generates an HMAC embedded in the event message body (compare HMAC computed over the message body), and optionally AES-128/256-encrypts the message (base64-encoded). Delivery is x-www-form-urlencoded POST, not JSON
dedup_mechanism: No delivery-id documented; consumers key on ResponseID/SurveyID fields in the form-encoded payload
learnings: Mostly an anti-pattern catalog for attune: form-encoded (non-JSON) delivery, a single topic string instead of an events array, body-embedded HMAC instead of a signed header, and brand-admin-only subscription all add integrator friction — its Zapier app consequently has zero instant triggers and polls instead. The one idea worth keeping is wildcard topic patterns (prefix.* ) for subscribe-to-everything-in-a-family.

name: Jotform
zapier_auth: Login-based connect flow ('Log into Jotform to authenticate, grant Zapier permission'), with a European-datacenter selection question — OAuth-style session grant, not a pasted API key
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.jotform.com/form/{formID}/webhooks with form-encoded webhookURL param; GET same path lists; DELETE /form/{formID}/webhooks/{webhookID}; auth via apiKey query param or APIKEY header
event_filtering: per-form endpoint, no event-type vocabulary at all — a webhook on a form receives every new submission for that form
signature_scheme: None documented — no signature header or HMAC mentioned in the API docs or the webhook help article
dedup_mechanism: No delivery-id/event-id documented; consumers key on submissionID in the payload
learnings: Shows the minimum viable per-resource webhook (one URL param, no events array) is enough to power a Zapier Instant trigger, but under-specifying costs later: no signature, no event types, no retry contract documented. attune should ship signatures and an event-type array from day one rather than retrofitting.

name: Tally
zapier_auth: Login-based connect flow ('Log into Tally to authenticate, grant Zapier permission') — OAuth-style grant
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.tally.so/webhooks (Bearer token) with JSON {formId, url, eventTypes:["FORM_RESPONSE"], signingSecret, httpHeaders:[{name,value}], externalSubscriber}; also PATCH/DELETE /webhooks/{id}, GET webhook events, POST retry webhook events
event_filtering: eventTypes array per subscription (currently a single enum value FORM_RESPONSE), scoped to one formId
signature_scheme: Tally-Signature header = base64(HMAC-SHA256(signingSecret, JSON.stringify(payload))) — no timestamp in the signed content
retry_disable_policy: 10-second response timeout expecting 2XX; on failure 5 retries at 5 min, 30 min, 1 h, 6 h, 1 day; no auto-disable documented (webhooks can be paused manually; delivery event log with manual retry endpoint)
dedup_mechanism: eventId (UUID) plus eventType in the JSON payload
learnings: The cleanest small-vendor shape for attune to copy: one POST /webhooks endpoint taking url + eventTypes[] + caller-supplied signingSecret + custom httpHeaders, an externalSubscriber field to tag integration-created hooks (exactly what a Zapier connector needs for cleanup), an explicit documented retry ladder, and a delivery-events log with a manual retry API. Avoid its signature construction though — HMAC over re-stringified JSON without a timestamp is fragile and replayable; sign the raw body with a timestamp instead.

name: Formbricks
zapier_auth: API key — Formbricks' own Zapier guide walks through pasting an API key into the Zapier connection window (API v2 uses x-api-key header)
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://app.formbricks.com/api/v2/management/webhooks (x-api-key) with JSON {name, url, source: user|zapier|make|n8n, workspaceId, triggers:[...], surveyIds:[...]}; full CRUD (GET list/one, PUT, DELETE)
event_filtering: triggers array of event-type enums per subscription, additionally scoped by a surveyIds array — two-axis filtering (event type x resource)
signature_scheme: Standard Webhooks spec: webhook-id + webhook-timestamp + webhook-signature headers; signature = 'v1,' + base64(HMAC-SHA256(whsec_-prefixed secret, '{id}.{timestamp}.{body}')); server-generated secret returned at creation; 5-minute replay tolerance recommended
dedup_mechanism: webhook-id header (unique message identifier) plus webhookId and event fields in the JSON payload
learnings: The closest OSS analog to attune and the strongest template: adopt the Standard Webhooks signature scheme (interoperable client libraries in 8+ languages for free), the source enum tagging who created the subscription (user/zapier/make/n8n) which makes connector-owned webhooks auditable, and triggers[] x surveyIds[] two-axis filtering. Also note its SSRF guard: private/internal target IPs blocked by default with an explicit self-host escape hatch — directly relevant to attune's allow_loopback_egress design. Gap to avoid: no documented retry policy.

name: Stripe
zapier_auth: Connect-account flow: 'Yes, Continue to Stripe' then log into Stripe and grant Zapier access (OAuth-style); using test-mode data additionally requires creating a Stripe secret API key
webhook_sub_endpoint: POST https://api.stripe.com/v1/webhook_endpoints with url + enabled_events[] (repeated param), e.g. enabled_events[]=charge.succeeded; response includes the endpoint's signing secret (whsec_...); full CRUD on /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}
event_filtering: enabled_events array of event-type strings per endpoint (resource.action dot notation); each endpoint independently selects its event set
signature_scheme: Stripe-Signature header 't={ts},v1={sig}': HMAC-SHA256 over signed_payload '{timestamp}.{raw_body}' keyed by the endpoint's whsec_ secret; timestamp inside the signed payload defeats replay, libraries default to 5-minute tolerance; ignore non-v1 schemes to prevent downgrade
retry_disable_policy: Live mode: exponential backoff retries for up to 3 days; sandbox: 3 retries over a few hours; retries stop if the destination is disabled/deleted; manual resend up to 15 days (Dashboard) / 30 days (CLI); endpoints can be disabled via API (disabled flag) — no automatic-disable schedule stated in the retrieved docs
dedup_mechanism: Unique event id — docs instruct logging processed event IDs and skipping already-logged ones; for the rare two-distinct-Event duplicates, dedup on data.object id + event.type
learnings: The industry reference attune should copy almost verbatim: enabled_events[] per endpoint, resource.action dot-notation vocabulary, signing secret minted and returned at subscription creation, timestamp-inside-signature (t=/v1=) replay protection, days-long exponential retry, and explicit consumer guidance to dedup on event id and to return 2xx before doing work. Its Zapier app also shows the hidden-polling-trigger trick: hidden 'List X' polling reads feed dynamic dropdowns while user-facing triggers are REST hooks.

name: Shopify
zapier_auth: OAuth login flow: enter the store subdomain (from admin.shopify.com/store/{name}), 'Yes, Continue to Shopify', log in and grant access; the Zapier app is a Premium (paid-plan) integration
webhook_sub_endpoint: GraphQL Admin API webhookSubscriptionCreate mutation at POST /admin/api/{version}/graphql.json (topic enum e.g. ORDERS_CREATE + webhookSubscription{uri, format, includeFields, metafieldNamespaces}), or declarative app-config: [[webhooks.subscriptions]] topics=["products/update"] uri=... in shopify.app.toml; targets: HTTPS URL, Google Pub/Sub, or Amazon EventBridge
event_filtering: topic-based: one topic per subscription (resource/action slash notation; SCREAMING_CASE in GraphQL); TOML topics array expands to one subscription per topic; plus per-subscription payload shaping via filter and include_fields
signature_scheme: X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header: base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed by the app's client secret (HTTPS deliveries only; constant-time compare; up to 1 h of dual-secret validity after secret rotation)
retry_disable_policy: Failed deliveries retried up to 8 times within a 4-hour window; after repeated failures in a 24-hour period the subscription is removed — but only shop-specific (API-created) subscriptions are auto-deleted; app-specific (TOML-declared) subscriptions are never deleted by Shopify
dedup_mechanism: X-Shopify-Webhook-Id header (unique composite key per delivery, documented for dedup) plus X-Shopify-Event-Id (shared across all deliveries produced by the same merchant action); X-Shopify-Triggered-At timestamp
learnings: Copy the two-level ID design — a per-delivery Webhook-Id for consumer dedup distinct from a per-business-event Event-Id — and the metadata-header set (topic, API version, triggered-at). The 8-retries/4-hours then auto-remove policy is a concrete model for attune's disable-after-N-failures rule, with the nuance that config-declared subscriptions survive while API-created ones get culled. Avoid the dual event-name spelling (orders/create vs ORDERS_CREATE): attune should keep exactly one canonical event-token form, consistent with its append-only source vocabulary.
